experiences.title: Concise Date Offset Completeness Depends on Boundary Labels
experiences.description: Retrieve when evaluating a Matplotlib ConciseDateFormatter trajectory that is modifying level/offset logic for same-year, sub-year date ranges, especially where January may or may not appear among ticks.
experiences.context: Applies in a Python/Matplotlib codebase when the task concerns concise date tick labels and the visible trajectory has reached the formatter’s batch tick-formatting logic, offset-string decisions, or tests for month-spanning ranges. It is most relevant once the agent is proposing or validating a fix involving level selection, offset suppression, zero/boundary formats, or January/month-start behavior. It is less useful during initial repository search, for unrelated date locator bugs, or when the trajectory has only produced environment/import troubleshooting without inspecting how tick labels and offset text share date context. Do not apply it as a generic demand that every sub-year plot have a non-empty offset; the key boundary is whether the year is already made visible by a boundary tick label such as January.
experiences.experience: Previous rubrics in this cluster often asked for the original reported plot to show the year in the offset and to preserve general concise formatting. That is directionally useful, but it can be too weak: a trajectory can make the reported case appear to contain a year while still missing the precise ConciseDateFormatter contract, or can accept misleading outputs caused by timezone/DST hour variation, manual scalar formatter calls, or testing against an installed package rather than the edited source. A better rubric should focus on the semantic completeness rule: when month labels vary within one year and no tick label will itself show the year, the formatter must put the common year in the offset; when a boundary tick such as January already causes the year to be shown in the tick labels, the formatter should not add redundant or stale offset text. The criterion should reward visible reasoning about the interaction between level selection, offset suppression, and boundary/zero formats, not merely a one-line broad condition change or an assertion that the offset is non-empty in the original reproduction. Prioritize evidence that the agent inspects tick component uniqueness, recognizes January/month value as the year-bearing boundary case, validates both no-January and January-present ranges, and avoids replacing meaningful month/day labels with hour labels due to lower-level timezone artifacts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Boundary-Aware Year Offset Contract
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should demonstrate a precise ConciseDateFormatter fix or plan in which date context is complete but not redundant: for same-year ranges where the visible tick labels vary by month and do not include a year-bearing boundary tick, the common year is shown once in the offset; for ranges where a boundary tick label already displays the year, offset suppression/clearing behavior is preserved. The judgment should be based on visible reasoning, code changes, or tests that connect level selection, boundary/zero-format labels, and offset text, rather than on a single reproduction output or misleading scalar formatting calls.

required_visible_evidence: Identifies that concise formatter completeness depends on whether the year appears in either tick labels or offset text
Distinguishes month-spanning same-year ranges without January from ranges containing January or year-changing ticks
Accounts for boundary/zero-format behavior where January can make the year visible in a tick label
Validates or proposes tests for both no-January and January-present cases
Avoids relying solely on manual scalar formatter calls, unrelated installed-package behavior, or DST-induced hour labels as proof of correctness
common_false_positives: Only checks that the original reproduction has some offset containing the year
Changes offset suppression broadly without considering whether a tick label already contains the year
Forces coarser month labeling in a way that may override legitimate day/hour/minute granularity
Treats timezone/DST lower-level variation as the main semantic fix instead of preserving the formatter’s context-sharing contract

scale.1: No meaningful evidence that the trajectory understands the year must appear exactly somewhere across tick labels and offset, or it remains focused on unrelated setup/import issues.
scale.2: Recognizes the missing-year symptom or locates formatter offset logic, but only proposes a broad non-empty-offset fix or validates the original case without considering January/boundary-label behavior.
scale.3: Shows moderate understanding of month-level offset suppression and the need to preserve concise labels, but lacks clear evidence that January or other year-bearing boundary labels are handled separately.
scale.4: Clearly reasons that no-January same-year month ranges need the year in the offset while January-present ranges may already display the year in tick labels, and proposes corresponding validation.
scale.5: Provides strong, boundary-aware evidence through implementation reasoning and/or tests covering no-January, January-present, year-changing, and finer-granularity cases, while explicitly avoiding misleading scalar-call or timezone-artifact validation.

experiences.title: Django grouped queryset default-ordering suppression
experiences.description: Retrieve when a Django ORM task concerns `QuerySet.ordered` disagreeing with generated SQL for annotated/aggregate `GROUP BY` queries on models with `Meta.ordering`.
experiences.context: Hard applicability gate: use this experience only when the task visibly concerns `QuerySet.ordered`, model `Meta.ordering`, and aggregate `GROUP BY` SQL suppressing default ordering. Do not generate, adapt, or analogize a rubric from this card for queryset pickling, result iterable selection, `values()` result shape, or any ordering-independent ORM bug. When the gate is not visibly satisfied, this experience contributes no rubric; derive criteria from the task and other applicable experiences instead. Applies in a Django source tree when the visible task and trajectory involve the `QuerySet.ordered` property, aggregate annotations or `values().annotate()` causing `query.group_by`, and the distinction between model default ordering and explicit `order_by()`. The criterion is most useful after the agent has at least located `QuerySet.ordered` or investigated SQL compiler/query ordering behavior; it can still flag early trajectories that are only repeating searches without understanding the semantic boundary. Do not apply broadly to unrelated ordering bugs, to SQL generation changes where the desired fix is to preserve `ORDER BY`, or to cases where ordering is explicit via `order_by()`/`extra_order_by` rather than coming only from `Meta.ordering`.
experiences.experience:
The useful rubrics in this cluster focused on the specific semantic contract: grouped aggregate querysets should not be considered ordered solely because `query.default_ordering` and model `Meta.ordering` are true, since Django’s compiler suppresses default/meta ordering when emitting `GROUP BY`; however explicit ordering must still make the queryset ordered. This criterion aligned well because visible trajectories that inspected compiler behavior, reproduced `group_by` with no SQL `ORDER BY`, or patched the default-ordering branch of `QuerySet.ordered` had decisive evidence of likely correctness, while trajectories stuck repeating greps lacked such evidence. A better rubric should not merely reward finding `default_ordering` or `group_by` strings; it should require recognizing the interaction among `query.group_by`, default `Meta.ordering`, and explicit ordering preservation. Avoid tempting but wrong criteria such as “all annotated queries are unordered,” “set `default_ordering` to false during annotation,” or “tests passed” without checking the behavioral boundary. Prioritize visible evidence that the agent compared `.ordered` with actual SQL, identified that compiler suppression applies only to meta/default ordering, and implemented or planned a minimal change in the introspection property rather than altering unrelated SQL generation.

This card has a binding applicability gate. Shared repository, ORM vocabulary, or incidental mention of one keyword is insufficient. If every gate marker is not visible, ignore this card completely rather than transferring its rubric semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Only under the exact applicability gate: Default meta ordering suppressed by GROUP BY
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Generate this criterion only when the task visibly concerns `QuerySet.ordered`, model `Meta.ordering`, and aggregate `GROUP BY` SQL suppressing default ordering. Otherwise do not generate it. Rewards trajectories that correctly handle Django grouped queryset ordering introspection: `QuerySet.ordered` should return false when a queryset has `GROUP BY` from aggregate annotation/values grouping and its only possible ordering is model `Meta.ordering`, because the compiled SQL omits that default `ORDER BY`; explicit `order_by()` or `extra_order_by`, non-grouped default-ordered querysets, and empty querysets should retain their existing ordered behavior.

key_state: query.group_by is truthy for aggregate/grouped querysets
query.default_ordering can remain true despite SQL lacking ORDER BY
query.order_by or query.extra_order_by indicates explicit ordering that should remain ordered
preferred_visible_evidence: inspection of QuerySet.ordered default-ordering branch
inspection or reproduction showing compiler drops Meta.ordering for GROUP BY SQL
manual or formal checks comparing .ordered and generated SQL
patch or plan that adds a not-grouped condition only to the default Meta.ordering path
boundaries: do not mark explicit order_by grouped querysets unordered
do not require changing SQL compilation to add ORDER BY
do not treat repeated grep output as sufficient understanding

scale.1: No meaningful evidence that the trajectory understands or addresses the grouped-query/default-ordering mismatch; it may only repeat searches or discuss ordering generically.
scale.2: Weak evidence: the trajectory locates `QuerySet.ordered`, `default_ordering`, or `group_by`, but does not connect grouped aggregate queries to suppression of default `Meta.ordering` in emitted SQL.
scale.3: Moderate evidence: the trajectory identifies that aggregate annotations create `GROUP BY` and that `.ordered` can disagree with SQL, but the proposed fix or investigation is incomplete or risks treating explicit ordering/default ordering incorrectly.
scale.4: Strong evidence: the trajectory clearly distinguishes default `Meta.ordering` from explicit ordering and proposes or applies a targeted `QuerySet.ordered` change so grouped queries relying only on defaults are unordered.
scale.5: Strongest evidence: the trajectory demonstrates the compiler/introspection mismatch with SQL or tests, applies a minimal fix in the default-ordering branch, preserves explicit and non-grouped ordering behavior, and validates relevant regression cases.

experiences.title: Preserve Exact Numeric Types Before Formatting
experiences.description: Use this when a formatting/filter bug is caused by converting an already-exact numeric value, such as a Decimal, through an imprecise representation before rounding or rendering.
experiences.context: Applies in Python/Django-like template or formatting code when the task explicitly reports precision loss for Decimal or other exact numeric inputs, and the visible trajectory has located the input-normalization path or is editing it. It is especially relevant once the agent has observed that a parse failure or fallback path sends the exact value through binary float conversion. It is less useful for unrelated display-format bugs, localization-only issues, or very early exploration before the conversion mechanism is visible. At final-review stages, the criterion should judge the semantic conversion behavior more than whether the agent added a formal regression test, unless the task specifically requires test changes.
experiences.experience: The useful rubrics in these cases focused on the core semantic contract: the formatting filter must build its internal Decimal from the original exact value, or from a precision-preserving string form, and must not route Decimal inputs through float. This aligned well because the visible trajectory repeatedly showed decisive evidence: the agent reproduced the precision loss, identified that repr-like conversion of Decimal was not directly parseable, found the fallback to float, and patched that conversion path while smoke-testing high-precision Decimal output and common formatting variants. A better rubric should ask whether the trajectory preserves exact Decimal digits while maintaining existing behavior for floats, strings, ints, rounding, and grouping/localization suffixes. Avoid making a project-native regression test the primary criterion in this situation: adding a test is valuable, but a code-only semantic fix can still address the task, and a test-focused rubric may understate a correct trajectory. Also avoid broad proxies such as “ran many tests” or “changed the filter file”; prioritize visible evidence that the lossy conversion path is removed or bypassed for exact numeric inputs and that fallback behavior remains available for non-Decimal inputs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact Decimal Conversion Preservation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should demonstrate that the formatting/filter implementation preserves exact Decimal precision by avoiding any Decimal-to-float conversion for Decimal inputs, using the original Decimal value or a precision-preserving textual representation before rounding and rendering, while keeping existing behavior for non-Decimal inputs and format options intact.

prioritize_evidence: The agent identifies a lossy conversion or fallback path involving binary float.
The proposed or applied edit bypasses that path for Decimal/exact numeric inputs.
The trajectory validates high-precision Decimal rendering with the requested number of places.
The trajectory considers preservation of existing behavior for other numeric/string inputs and formatting suffixes.
avoid_as_primary_evidence: Only adding a regression test without fixing the conversion path.
Only running broad test suites without inspecting the numeric conversion semantics.
Changing unrelated formatting or localization behavior as a proxy for precision preservation.

scale.1: No meaningful evidence that the agent understands or addresses the lossy exact-numeric conversion; the trajectory may focus on unrelated formatting behavior.
scale.2: Weak evidence: the agent reproduces the precision issue or mentions float precision loss, but has not located or changed the conversion path that causes Decimal inputs to lose digits.
scale.3: Moderate evidence: the agent identifies the lossy conversion path and proposes a plausible precision-preserving approach, but implementation or validation is incomplete or does not clearly cover preservation of existing non-Decimal behavior.
scale.4: Strong evidence: the agent patches or clearly plans a patch so Decimal inputs avoid binary float conversion, and validates the reported high-precision case while showing awareness of non-Decimal compatibility.
scale.5: Strongest evidence: the trajectory decisively removes or bypasses the lossy path for Decimal inputs, preserves fallback behavior for other inputs, and validates both the reported high-precision rendering and representative existing formatting behaviors such as rounding, strings/ints/floats, and grouping/localization options.

experiences.title: Require upstream surd-domain validation, not just empty-helper guards
experiences.description: Use for SymPy/symbolic-denesting trajectories where an IndexError arises from an empty surd list in a low-level helper, but the caller may be invoking surd-splitting on expressions outside its mathematical domain.
experiences.context: Applies in Python symbolic algebra tasks involving square-root denesting or radical simplification, especially when the visible traceback reaches a helper that assumes a nonempty list after a caller filters terms into surds. The key matching evidence is that the agent has inspected a caller like a sqrt-matching routine, observed a broad predicate such as 'all term squares are rational', and found that complex or imaginary terms can satisfy it while not being valid positive-radicand surds. This guidance is most useful after the trajectory has enough code inspection to distinguish caller eligibility from helper robustness. It is less applicable to generic empty-list crashes where the helper is explicitly documented to accept empty input, or to early exploration before the agent has inspected the caller's domain checks.
experiences.experience: The tempting rubric in these cases is to require an empty-input guard in the low-level gcd/surd helper or a neutral return from the splitter. That criterion can look plausible because it prevents the immediate IndexError, and it may correctly flag trajectories that have made no implementation progress. However, it is not a reliable semantic criterion once the agent starts patching: a neutral empty-helper return can hide the crash while allowing the denesting algorithm to treat non-surd complex sums as valid radical matches. The better rubric should focus on whether the trajectory recognizes and fixes the upstream domain boundary: surd splitting should only be attempted for additive terms whose squared values are positive rationals/valid surd radicands, while expressions with imaginary or non-positive rational squares should be treated as non-denestable and returned unchanged. Prioritize visible evidence such as: inspection of the caller predicate that admits too many expressions; recognition that terms like imaginary components have rational but non-positive squares; comments or tests showing the splitter is intended for positive-rational surds; a change or planned change that narrows the caller's eligibility before invoking surd grouping; and validation that known denestable radicals still denest while non-denestable complex expressions no longer crash. Avoid rewarding mere direct helper tests, repeated public calls that simplify away the problematic structure, or a patch that only makes the empty helper return a default tuple.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Upstream surd-domain eligibility is corrected
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should identify and address the mathematical-domain error that lets the denesting matcher call surd-splitting on additive expressions whose term squares are rational but not positive-rational surd radicands. Strong evidence includes narrowing the caller-side condition before surd splitting, treating complex/non-positive-square sums as non-denestable so the public denesting API returns them unchanged, and preserving successful denesting for valid radical inputs. A low-level empty-input guard alone is insufficient unless paired with evidence that the upstream matcher no longer classifies invalid complex sums as surd-splittable.

metadata.visible_failure_shape: IndexError from helper called with an empty surd collection
metadata.semantic_boundary: surd splitting is valid for positive-rational radicand terms, not merely any terms whose squares are rational
preferred_evidence: recognition of non-positive or imaginary square cases
caller-side domain narrowing or equivalent non-denestable fallback
tests for non-crash/unchanged behavior and preservation of valid denesting
avoid_as_primary_evidence: only adding an empty varargs/list guard to the helper
only checking that direct helper calls no longer raise
using an original reproducer that auto-simplifies before reaching the buggy path

scale.1: No evidence that the trajectory distinguishes caller-domain validation from the low-level empty-list crash; it only repeats reproduction attempts or focuses on unrelated behavior.
scale.2: The trajectory notices the empty surd list or helper crash but frames the solution only as an empty-input guard, with no recognition that the caller is accepting invalid non-positive/complex terms.
scale.3: The trajectory partially recognizes that some non-surd expressions are being routed into surd splitting, but the proposed fix or tests still center on neutral helper returns rather than a clear upstream eligibility boundary.
scale.4: The trajectory clearly identifies that the matcher's eligibility predicate is too broad and proposes or implements narrowing before surd splitting, with some validation that non-denestable complex expressions pass through unchanged.
scale.5: The trajectory decisively fixes or plans the upstream domain check for positive-rational surd terms, avoids relying on helper defaults as the main solution, and validates both non-denestable complex/no-surd cases and existing valid denesting behavior.

experiences.title: Autodoc Mock Generic Subscription Name Normalization
experiences.description: Retrieve when a Python documentation/mock-import bug involves generic typing objects, especially TypeVar, reaching dynamic mock name or subclass creation and causing string concatenation/type-name failures.
experiences.context: Applies in Python codebases with autodoc-style mocked imports or dynamic mock objects, when the task or trajectory visibly connects a generic typed class, TypeVar, or typing subscription to a mock object name-building path. It is most useful once the agent has located the dynamic mock factory or subscription/attribute access call path and can see non-string values being used as names. It is less useful for unrelated TypeVar rendering/documenter bugs, real import-resolution failures, or early exploration before the trajectory has tied the crash to mock subscription/name creation rather than general dependency setup.
experiences.experience: The useful rubrics in these cases focused on the semantic boundary that matters: generic subscription keys are not guaranteed to be strings, but mock subclass/display-name construction assumes strings. A good rubric should reward evidence that the agent identifies the mock generic-subscription path, normalizes non-string typing inputs before string concatenation or dynamic class creation, and preserves ordinary mocked attribute/name behavior. Visible evidence to prioritize includes finding the `module + '.' + name`-style failure, tracing calls from mock item access or dynamic subclass creation, reproducing the TypeError with `TypeVar('T')`, observing that `str(TypeVar)` is safe, applying a narrow normalization at the caller or helper that covers the failing path, and running focused checks such as a mocked object indexed by a TypeVar plus existing mock tests. Avoid generating a broad criterion about all generic/typehint rendering, dependency installation, or the external docs project build; those are tempting proxies but do not directly predict whether the mock crash is fixed. Also avoid over-constraining the exact patch location or exact display spelling unless visible tests require it: the judgeable requirement is that non-string generic names are converted safely and normal string-name behavior remains intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Type-Safe Generic Names in Mock Subclass Creation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should demonstrate that the agent is fixing the mock-object generic subscription/name path by safely converting TypeVar or other non-string typing objects into usable string names before they are used in display-name concatenation or dynamic class creation, while preserving existing behavior for normal string attribute access and validating the failing TypeVar scenario.

required_visible_evidence: Identifies the dynamic mock subclass or display-name construction that assumes a string name
Connects TypeVar or generic subscription to the non-string name argument
Implements or plans a narrow normalization of non-string generic keys/names
Checks that normal string mock attributes still behave as before
Uses a focused TypeVar/mock subscription reproduction or regression test when feasible
avoid_as_primary_evidence: Only inspecting general TypeVar documenter/typehint rendering code
Only attempting the external project docs build without isolating the mock failure

scale.1: No meaningful evidence that the trajectory addresses non-string generic values in the mock name/subclass path.
scale.2: Recognizes TypeVar or generics are involved but does not clearly connect them to mock subscription/name construction or proposes only broad unrelated changes.
scale.3: Identifies the string-concatenation/name assumption and the need to handle TypeVar, but implementation or validation of the actual mock subscription path is incomplete.
scale.4: Clearly normalizes TypeVar or other non-string generic names in the relevant mock path and shows focused validation, with only minor uncertainty about coverage or regression testing.
scale.5: Precisely traces the generic subscription path, applies a minimal safe normalization before display-name/dynamic-class use, preserves ordinary mock behavior, and validates both the TypeVar failure case and existing mock behavior.

experiences.title: Do not reward nominal refactor scaffolding without behavior-preserving integration
experiences.description: Retrieve when generating rubrics for a large Python refactor task that names desired architecture elements, especially when the visible trajectory shows only exploration, broad rewrites, class scaffolding, or partial test repair.
experiences.context: This applies to Open Library-style Solr update pipeline refactors in Python where the task explicitly asks for a unified state object and dedicated updater classes. A misleading criterion merely checks that named classes such as a state object and work/author/edition updaters exist, or that the agent has understood the old monolithic structure. That idea is only useful as a small subcriterion after there is visible evidence of a coherent implementation. It should not be the primary rubric during early repository inspection, after repeated failed heredocs/partial rewrites, when tests are still failing, or when broad edits may have damaged legacy behavior. In these situations, the visible risk is not absence of class names; it is whether the refactor preserves Solr request serialization, public API compatibility, update orchestration semantics, and locked-down document-building behavior.
experiences.experience: The previous rubrics restated the task-specific architecture request: introduce a unified update state, add dedicated updater classes, and make update_keys aggregate their results. This is directionally related to the issue, but it becomes misleading when used as the main success predictor. In several trajectories, the agent either only inspected files, produced partial or failed edits, or added classes with the expected names while leaving behavior broken or unvalidated. A better rubric should focus on behavior-preserving integration: whether the new state object is the real request representation used by solr_update/update_keys, whether updater classes preserve existing work, edition, and author semantics, whether public imports and CLI callers remain compatible or are deliberately migrated, and whether targeted tests or import checks demonstrate no regressions. Avoid the tempting criterion that class names or architectural intent alone are enough. Prioritize visible evidence such as passing targeted Solr tests, successful import/compile checks, reviewed diffs around request serialization and update_keys, and explicit handling of redirects, orphan editions/synthetic works, author stats, output modes, commits, and document fields.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Nominal architecture without behavioral preservation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalize a trajectory for treating the requested refactor as satisfied by adding or planning named architecture elements without visible evidence that the new pipeline preserves the legacy Solr update contract. This flaw is present when the agent mainly introduces SolrUpdateState/updater scaffolding or delegates to a new module, but does not demonstrate that request serialization, update_keys orchestration, work/edition/author edge cases, public imports, output modes, commits, and document-building behavior remain intact. The flaw is especially severe if the trajectory shows broad manual rewrites, failed syntax/import/test collection, unresolved failing targeted tests, or ad hoc fixes to regressions caused by the refactor.

metadata.repository_context: Python Open Library Solr update refactor involving a large update_work module, Solr request serialization, update_keys orchestration, and tests under openlibrary/tests/solr.
metadata.misleading_proxy_to_avoid: Presence of named classes/state objects or high-level architecture understanding by itself.
preferred_visible_evidence: Targeted Solr tests or equivalent behavior checks pass after the refactor
Public imports and CLI/batch callers remain compatible or are explicitly migrated
Solr request JSON generation and retry/error behavior remain covered
update_keys still handles works, editions, authors, redirects, deletions, commits, output modes, and synthetic work cases
Document-building fields remain preserved rather than rewritten wholesale

scale.1: No evidence of this flaw: the trajectory ties the new architecture to concrete behavior preservation, validates targeted tests/imports, and reviews high-risk update paths.
scale.2: Minor evidence: named architecture is emphasized, but the trajectory also includes some meaningful compatibility checks or targeted validation.
scale.3: Moderate evidence: the trajectory has partial scaffolding plus limited validation, but important update paths or public API compatibility remain unexamined.
scale.4: Clear evidence: the trajectory mostly adds/plans state/updater classes or delegates to new code while tests, imports, serialization, or edge-case behavior are missing or unresolved.
scale.5: Most severe evidence: broad or partial rewrites introduce syntax/import/test failures or known behavior regressions, yet the trajectory still appears to rely on the presence of the requested class names as proof of completion.

experiences.title: Qualified Paths for Nested Classmethod Serialization
experiences.description: Retrieve when a Django migration serialization task concerns a classmethod or callable default defined on a nested class, especially when the trajectory has inspected callable serialization and Python name/qualname behavior.
experiences.context: Applies in a Python/Django codebase where migration files serialize callable references such as Field.default values. The useful stage is after the trajectory has either found the migration callable serializer branch for bound classmethods or has reproduced that a nested classmethod is emitted without its containing class. It is strongest when visible evidence includes Python introspection showing simple class names omit outer classes, serializer output before/after, or checks for top-level functions/classmethods and deeper nesting. It may be premature if the agent is only exploring repository structure with no evidence about callable serialization, and it may be irrelevant for bugs in model field defaults, database backends, enum value behavior, static methods, or serialization of classes themselves rather than classmethods bound to nested classes.
experiences.experience: The prior rubrics were useful because they judged the exact semantic contract that determines correctness here: a bound classmethod used in a migration must serialize to an importable dotted path containing the module, every containing class, the nested class, and the method name. The discriminative evidence was not merely that the agent edited a migration file or ran many tests; it was that the trajectory identified the bound-classmethod serialization path, recognized that the owner class's simple name drops lexical nesting, and changed/validated the class component so nested paths such as Outer.Inner.method are preserved while top-level functions and classmethods still serialize normally. A better rubric for similar cases should focus on observable proof of this qualified-path behavior and compatibility boundary: before/after serializer output, use of the class's qualified name for the bound owner, preservation of the existing module import set, and sanity checks for non-nested and deeper-nested cases. Avoid tempting but weaker criteria such as requiring ArrayField-specific handling, TextChoices-specific handling, broad migration autodetector changes, dependency installation progress, or simply running unrelated Django tests. Those may support confidence but do not establish the core serialization contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Nested Classmethod Qualified Serialization
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should demonstrate that migration serialization of a classmethod bound to a nested class emits the full importable qualified path including all containing classes, while preserving existing callable serialization behavior for ordinary functions, top-level classmethods, deeper nesting, and module imports. Strong evidence includes identifying the bound-classmethod serializer branch, explaining why the owner class's simple name is insufficient for nested classes, applying a targeted change to use the owner class's qualified path, and validating serializer output for nested and non-nested cases.

metadata.core_contract: Bound classmethods on nested classes serialize as module.Outer.Inner.method rather than module.Inner.method.
preferred_visible_evidence: Inspection of the callable or function serializer branch that handles methods whose __self__ is a class
Python introspection or reasoning showing __name__ omits outer classes while __qualname__ preserves them
A targeted source change in the classmethod serialization path rather than ArrayField-, enum-, or database-specific code
Serializer output before and after showing the containing class path appears in the serialized value
Checks that ordinary functions, top-level classmethods, deeper nested classmethods, and imports remain compatible
avoid_as_primary_evidence: Running unrelated test suites without checking serialized output
Changing migration autodetection or field default evaluation instead of callable reference serialization
Only proving TextChoices or ArrayField behavior without addressing the generic nested classmethod path

scale.1: No visible evidence that the trajectory understands or addresses nested classmethod serialization; it focuses on unrelated field, enum, database, or test-environment issues.
scale.2: Some recognition that migrations serialize callable defaults, but no clear identification of the bound-classmethod path or the missing containing-class qualification.
scale.3: Identifies that nested class names are being lost in migration serialization and may propose qualified names, but validation or compatibility evidence for non-nested callables is limited.
scale.4: Clearly targets the bound-classmethod serializer path, uses the owner class's qualified path, and shows serializer output now includes the containing class for a nested classmethod.
scale.5: Provides decisive evidence for the full contract: targeted qualified-path fix, before/after nested classmethod serialization, preservation of module imports, and sanity checks for ordinary functions, top-level classmethods, and deeper nested classmethods.

experiences.title: Iterator Contract for Paginator-Like Containers
experiences.description: Use when a Python task explicitly asks to make a container/paginator object iterable by adding `__iter__`, and the visible trajectory has identified the target class plus existing page-range and page-construction APIs.
experiences.context: Applies in a Python/Django-style codebase when the problem statement is narrow: implement normal iteration over an existing paginator-like class. The trajectory should show evidence such as locating the class, inspecting the existing `page_range`/range API and `page()`/page-construction method, or testing that direct iteration currently fails while manual iteration through page numbers works. This criterion is most useful once the agent is at implementation or review stage; it may be premature during pure repository exploration before the target class and existing APIs are visible. It is less applicable if the task asks for a broader redesign of pagination, iteration over raw objects rather than pages, async iteration, custom sequence behavior, or changes to page numbering/validation semantics.
experiences.experience: The useful rubrics in these cases focused on the actual semantic contract: `__iter__` must be added to the paginator class and each fresh iteration must yield the existing `Page` objects produced by calling the existing page-construction method for every number in the existing page-range property. This aligned well because the task itself supplied the intended implementation and the trajectory exposed decisive evidence: manual loops over `page_range` plus `page()` worked, direct iteration failed before the change, and successful edits inserted a generator method without changing surrounding pagination behavior. A better rubric should judge whether the implementation preserves existing pagination semantics, including empty paginator, orphan handling, single-page cases, and repeated iteration, by delegating to `page_range` and `page()` rather than reimplementing slicing or validation. Avoid tempting but weaker criteria such as requiring a particular insertion line, docstring wording, full test-suite execution, adding new tests, comparing `Page` objects by equality, or merely checking that some `__iter__` method exists. Also avoid rewarding implementations that return page numbers, raw object lists, a one-time stored iterator, or modify `page_range`/`page()` to make tests pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Paginator Iterator Delegates to Existing Page Semantics
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should implement the Python iterator protocol on the paginator-like class by adding `__iter__` as a fresh generator that loops over the existing page-number range and yields the existing page object for each page number, while leaving existing page-count, range, validation, orphan, and empty-page behavior unchanged.

required_visible_evidence: The target class has been identified as the paginator-like class requested by the task.
The class already exposes an existing page-number range API and an existing method that constructs/returns page objects.
The proposed or applied implementation adds `__iter__` to that class, not to the page class or an unrelated helper.
`__iter__` iterates over the existing page-number range and yields the result of the existing page-construction method for each number.
The trajectory does not show semantic changes to page numbering, validation, slicing, orphan handling, or empty-page behavior.
anti_patterns: Yielding raw items, object-list slices, or page numbers instead of page objects.
Returning a list rather than providing a normal reusable iteration protocol.
Using a stored one-shot iterator that would break repeated iteration.
Reimplementing pagination calculations inside `__iter__` instead of delegating to existing APIs.
Changing existing `page_range`, `page()`, validation, or page-count behavior to support iteration.
metadata.stage_notes: Before any implementation is visible, judge mostly on whether the agent has identified the correct contract and target APIs. After an edit is visible, prioritize the actual method body and absence of collateral semantic changes over test-run completeness.

scale.1: No meaningful evidence that the trajectory is implementing the requested iterator contract, or it targets the wrong class/API.
scale.2: Some recognition that the paginator should be iterable, but the visible plan or code is incomplete, ambiguous, or likely to yield the wrong type of value.
scale.3: The trajectory is approximately on track relative to the parent state, but the implementation evidence is partial or does not yet clearly prove delegation to the existing page-range and page-construction APIs.
scale.4: Clear evidence of an added `__iter__` on the correct class that loops through the existing page range and yields pages, with little sign of collateral behavior changes.
scale.5: Strongest evidence: the correct generator-style `__iter__` is visible, it delegates exactly to the existing page-range and page-construction behavior, repeated/edge-case iteration is considered or tested, and no unrelated pagination semantics are changed.

experiences.title: Mpmath Rational fixes: conversion ordering and dependency compatibility outrank local test volume
experiences.description: When ranking Rational serialization fixes in an mpmath printer, distinguish precision-safe, primitive API usage from invalid two-argument calls, conversion after native division, and parser-dependent shorthand. A successful reproduction under a freshly installed dependency is useful but does not erase compatibility differences between implementations.
experiences.context: The target printer must emit Rational constants without first evaluating numerator/denominator division as a native float. Visible candidates include `mpf(p)/mpf(q)`, `mpf(p, q)`, `mpf(p/q)`, and `mpf('p/q')`. The view establishes that `mpf` accepts one value, that the two-argument form raises `TypeError`, and that separately converted operands retain precision. It also shows quoted fractional strings working in the locally installed dependency, but does not establish support across other dependency versions.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when a paused or completed trajectory edits or evaluates `MpmathPrinter._print_Rational`, particularly when candidates differ in how numerator and denominator reach mpmath.

Decisive positive evidence: Generated code converts operands before division, for example `mpf(-232)/mpf(3)`, and executes at elevated precision. This relies only on one-argument conversion plus mpmath arithmetic. Accept any behaviorally equivalent construction whose supported API and precision are visibly established; do not require exact formatting, qualification, or aliases.

Decisive contradictory evidence: `mpf(p, q)` is invalid when the visible run raises `TypeError`. `mpf(p/q)` is precision-losing because native division happens before conversion. Syntax errors, an unexecuted malformed expression, or the known degraded decimal also contradict correctness.

Qualified evidence: `mpf('p/q')` visibly working under a freshly installed dependency proves the local case, so it must not be treated as no progress. However, absent visible dependency-range support, that parser shorthand is weaker compatibility evidence than constructing two one-argument values and dividing them. Exact local reproduction and generic passing tests cannot by themselves close this compatibility question.

Close-looking exclusions: A mere `mpf` token does not prove correct operation ordering. Generic mpmath tests may never exercise Rational serialization. Missing optional packages are unrelated. An explicit `q == 1` branch is usually immaterial when denominator-one values are canonicalized to Integer before Rational dispatch. Fully qualified `mpmath.mpf` and imported `mpf` are equivalent.

Abstention boundary: If the generated expression or executed behavior is truncated, do not infer conversion ordering. If no supported dependency range is visible, do not categorically reject quoted fractional strings; record them as locally validated but compatibility-unproven. If an alternative implementation visibly establishes both precision and supported-API compatibility, preserve it as equivalent.

Rejected weighting: Do not rank primarily by the number of green tests or by one exact high-precision run against an ad hoc dependency installation. Those are supporting signals. The decisive ranking evidence is whether conversion occurs before division, whether the called API is valid, and whether any parser-dependent representation is visibly compatible with the intended environment.

experiences.title: Rank per-artist text antialiasing by the observed core state-transfer path, not parser API breadth
experiences.description: When paused prefixes for per-artist text antialiasing compete, prioritize visibly verified artist state, GraphicsContext transfer, and backend consumption. Do not elevate speculative MathTextParser or internal raster API changes above branches that display the primary contract in source.
experiences.context: Applies when the requested change adds antialiasing accessors to Text, uses a configured default when no explicit value is supplied, and replaces regular-text backend reads of the global setting with GraphicsContext state. It is especially relevant when all final summaries report no persisted patch or behavioral result, but command output differs between displaying core edits and merely reporting that patch scripts changed mathtext.py or _mathtext.py.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply when visible branches are paused without a persisted final diff or successful behavior check, and the comparison includes both core Text/GraphicsContext work and investigation or editing of MathTextParser, _parse_cached, to_raster, or glyph-raster internals. The observed rubric must be favoring downstream mathtext plumbing despite incomplete or unverified evidence for the primary artist-state path.

Decisive positive evidence: Rank the smallest visibly coherent vertical contract highest. Strong implementation evidence consists of source output showing (1) a Text antialiasing property exposed through get_antialiased and set_antialiased, with an unspecified value resolving to the configured text-antialiasing default and changes marking the artist stale; (2) Text.draw placing that value on the newly created GraphicsContext before invoking renderer text methods; and (3) affected regular-text backends obtaining the value from the GraphicsContext instead of directly reading the global setting. Credit each observed link at its actual stage, but reserve claims of end-to-end implementation for a visibly connected path. A separate Annotation edit is unnecessary when normal inheritance visibly supplies the property. Equivalent default resolution in the constructor, setter, getter, or an established property mechanism is valid. Likewise, transferring an equivalent stored value directly is acceptable if the public accessors and semantics remain coherent.

Contradictory evidence: A visible syntax defect, such as a missing comma before **kwargs, directly contradicts an executable implementation. So do a draw call to a getter that is visibly absent, a setter that does not establish the required default semantics, or a regular-text backend that still reads the global setting after per-artist state is claimed complete. Changing MathTextParser.parse, _parse_cached, VectorParse.to_raster, or related signatures without displaying all affected callers and preserved cache/default behavior expands an internal contract without demonstrating that the artist value reaches it. Such edits must not receive completion credit and may count negatively when a visible caller/signature mismatch is established.

Close-looking exclusions: A script printing that a file was patched is not the same as displaying the resulting source, particularly when the paused summary reports no patch. Grepping for the global setting, locating the internal glyph call, or reading draw_mathtext is useful diagnosis but not implementation. Merely exploring mathtext after establishing the core path is not harmful and should not lower a branch. Conversely, the number of internal layers inspected or edited is not a positive tiebreaker. Copying the property in update_from may be sensible follow-up work, but it must not outweigh the primary contract in this paused comparison. Failed environment setup neither validates nor disproves the source changes.

Explicit rejection of the misleading direction: Reject a positive rubric that gives dominant weight or high implementation levels merely for editing mathtext.py and _mathtext.py to thread an antialiased argument. In this state, parser/raster API breadth must not outrank observed Text accessors, GraphicsContext assignment, and regular-backend consumption. The direct global read in the mathtext raster path can justify later targeted work, but only after the core path is visibly established and the added API is supported by an actual caller trace or focused behavior check. Do not infer necessity or correctness from a larger downstream rewrite alone.

Abstention boundary: Because no persisted final diff or successful rendering check is visible, do not declare any prefix fully correct. If prefixes display equivalent portions of the core path, keep them tied rather than using mathtext exploration, command count, or file count as a tiebreaker. If edits are represented only by success messages or truncated output, abstain from implementation-quality ranking until resulting source is displayed. If a later prefix shows a coherent core path plus a connected and validated mathtext path, mathtext work may then receive additional credit without requiring one particular implementation location.

experiences.title: Rank Package.collect import-boundary fixes above pattern archaeology for arbitrary __init__.py collection
experiences.description: Use for the pytest 5.2.3 regression where collection imports an arbitrary package __init__.py, such as foobar/__init__.py containing an assertion, even though the file is outside the configured test-file patterns. In paused trajectories, judge the owner-level import ordering and local-source evidence rather than treating pattern greps or history browsing as the decisive diagnosis.
experiences.context: The visible source shows Package.collect calling self._mount_obj_if_needed() before inspecting init_module and applying path_matches_patterns. The mount path obtains the package object through the module import path, so collection can import __init__.py before the pattern decision. The visible reproduction reports an error collecting foobar/__init__.py, and one local change makes that specific error disappear but leaves a separate lineno-related failure. The task also requires retaining package skipping and legitimate collection behavior.
experiences.experience: Activation conditions: Apply when the visible task concerns arbitrary __init__.py imports during pytest collection and the trajectory is in diagnosis, reproduction, patch review, or paused pre-completion ranking. Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a continuation that identifies the ordering in Package.collect, explains that _mount_obj_if_needed leads to _getobj/_importtestmodule and therefore imports the package before pattern filtering, and targets the checked-out source. Stronger evidence includes a visible patch that removes, defers, or conditionally performs that mount without breaking package collection, plus a local-source reproduction in which the foobar/__init__.py collection error disappears. A residual error after that disappearance is useful causal evidence but limits completion credit unless the remaining behavior is also repaired. Preserve equivalent valid implementations; do not require one exact edit if an alternative maintains the same no-unconditional-import invariant and package skipping semantics. Contradictory evidence: Do not rank a continuation highest merely because it identifies parent.config.getini("python_files") + ["__init__.py"], quotes the pytest_collect_file hook, reports default glob patterns, or reconstructs commit history. Those observations do not establish that the earlier Package.collect mount is harmless and are insufficient without connecting them to the observed import timing. Also discount a green run against an installed package, a run with an unobservable import path, reproduction-file creation without execution, or a claimed fix with no visible source change. Close-looking exclusions: Pattern-hook inspection is meaningful supporting evidence when it is combined with Package.collect ordering analysis; history can explain why the mount was introduced but is not a substitute for active-source diagnosis. A local-source execution blocked by missing dependencies remains better-targeted evidence than a clean external-package run. A patch that removes the mount and eliminates the original __init__.py error but exposes a separate compatibility failure deserves partial positive credit, not completion credit and not zero credit. If no patch is visible, score diagnosis and targeting only and preserve uncertainty about eventual fix quality. Explicitly reject the misleading rubric direction that gives pattern archaeology or prompt-parroting higher weight than direct runtime-owner evidence: the decisive discriminator is the unconditional package import at the Package.collect boundary, while pattern analysis is secondary. Abstention boundary: If the visible output is truncated before the ordering of _mount_obj_if_needed and path_matches_patterns can be established, or if the execution target cannot be distinguished from an installed package, do not infer a completed fix or a failed approach. If the latest diff is unavailable, do not treat a reproduction result alone as proof of agent-improved behavior.

experiences.title: Parent-row identity proof outranks suite breadth for multi-table inheritance updates
experiences.description: When ranking fixes for a queryset update bug involving multiple inheritance, prioritize visible proof that the update selects the child-linked row in each affected parent table and does not modify unrelated standalone parent rows. Broad regression suites and data-structure elegance are supporting evidence only.
experiences.context: Activate for a multi-table or multiple-inheritance queryset update where a child update targets a field stored on a parent table and incorrect primary-key reuse can update unrelated parent instances. The diagnostic stage may include source exploration, a custom reproduction, targeted tests, or broader suite validation.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: The task involves updating inherited fields across parent tables, and visible branches differ in whether they demonstrate the final database state or merely report tests, inspect code, or describe a patch.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a branch that creates standalone records in the affected parent table before creating child records, thereby making the child’s first-parent primary key differ from the affected parent’s pointer values. After the update, it must visibly show or assert that every child-linked affected-parent row has the new value and every unrelated standalone parent row retains its old value. A targeted SQL predicate using the correct parent-pointer values is useful corroboration, but exact post-update object values are the decisive evidence. Strong secondary evidence covers filtered updates, updates to fields on multiple parents in one call, single-table inheritance, and ordinary models.

Decisive contradictory evidence: Treat visible modification of unrelated standalone parent rows, failure to modify child-linked parent rows, or an update predicate based on the wrong parent identity as a fix-breaking regression. Also downgrade a branch whose only support is a passing status, an update count, a self-reported success message, a patch artifact, or a broad suite run without output proving which rows changed. A suite can pass while missing this specific divergent-key scenario.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not treat equal primary-key values in a minimal fixture as proof of correctness; an incorrect child-key filter can appear to work when keys happen to coincide. Do not treat source inspection that finds parent links, a map of related values, or a plausible compiler path as behavioral validation. Do not require one particular representation such as a new map or a particular file split: equivalent valid implementations deserve equal treatment when the final row-selection contract is demonstrated. A returned count matching the number of children is insufficient unless the affected and unaffected value sets are also checked. Environment or test-discovery errors are not behavioral evidence either way.

Misleading rubric direction rejected: Do not weight generic test-suite breadth, the number of passing custom cases, method-name convergence, or auxiliary data-structure defensiveness above direct evidence of correct parent-row identity. Conversely, do not penalize a compact or structurally different implementation solely because it does not use the preferred map pattern. The observed audit error was allowing suite breadth and implementation neatness to outrank the visible reproduction showing the correct parent rows changed and unrelated rows did not.

Abstention boundary: If the visible prefix contains only code edits, test names, aggregate counts, truncated output, environment failures, or claims that tests passed without showing before/after values or assertions for both child-linked and standalone parent rows, do not infer the fix’s row-selection correctness. If the fixture does not establish divergent child and parent-pointer keys, keep candidates close because the central bug may be masked. Reserve implementation-completion credit until the relevant final state is visibly established.

experiences.title: Prioritize regression-safe Mul-branch localization over exact Mod patch imitation
experiences.description: Activate when evaluating a Mod simplification fix that must reduce an integer-coefficient product such as Mod(3*i, 2) while preserving float and symbolic behavior. Judge convergence on the correct branch boundary and visible regression results, not exact reproduction of a suggested diff or submission mechanics.
experiences.context: The visible task requires changing Mod.doit for the Mul case and adding the integer-symbol regression assertion, while preserving existing float behavior. The proposed unconditional transformation of every non-modulus factor can make expressions such as Mod(1.0*x, 1) evaluate to 0 and can cause recursion or float-test failures. The relevant distinction is a scoped Mul-branch repair versus broad or accidentally duplicated changes affecting Add or unrelated expressions.
experiences.experience: Positive evidence: the agent inspects the regression traceback or failing `test_Mod` assertion, identifies that the intended change belongs only under `elif isinstance(p, Mul):`, reverts an accidental Add-branch or otherwise broken edit, verifies the clean baseline, reapplies the change at the Mul boundary, and visibly reruns both the target reduction and the existing float-handling test. A valid implementation may differ from the suggested patch; preserve equivalent solutions that directly reduce the integer coefficient without changing non-integer or float semantics. Contradictory evidence: the agent keeps an unconditional `[cls(x, q) for x in non_mod_l]` transformation after observing `Mod(1.0*x, 1) -> 0`, recursion, or a failing float assertion; modifies the Add path; relies on a few passing custom examples while `test_Mod` fails; or submits an exact-looking diff without confirming regression safety. Explicitly reject the misleading rubric direction that exact PR-diff conformity, patch-file creation, successful target reproduction, or investigation thoroughness should outweigh visible regression failures. Close-looking exclusions: a brief mention of Add versus Mul is not enough without a diff or execution showing the boundary; reverting alone is not enough without a scoped reapplication or a clear valid alternative; a test command that fails only because of missing tooling is not evidence of a code regression; and a custom test labeled “all passed” does not override a visible failure in the existing Mod test. Abstain when the paused prefix contains no visible post-edit diff, no relevant test result, or ends before the agent can distinguish a temporary investigation state from a committed regression-safe direction.

experiences.title: Paused Text antialiasing task: prioritize the Text-to-GraphicsContext contract over MathText-only exploration
experiences.description: Use for paused, pre-implementation continuations for the per-artist Text antialiasing task when visible branches differ mainly in source inspection, edit scripts, and downstream rendering exploration, but no persisted patch is shown.
experiences.context: The visible task requires per-Text antialiasing with the existing global value as the default, transfer through GraphicsContext state, backend reads from that state, state propagation during artist copying, and compatible Annotation behavior. The judge view shows direct backend references, the existing GraphicsContext API, analogous Line2D or Patch patterns, Text initialization and draw sites, and a separate MathText reference. It also shows command outputs claiming edits while continuation summaries remain no-patch, so exploration, intent, and implementation must be scored separately.
experiences.experience: Activation conditions: Apply only when the task is the Text antialiasing change and the visible continuation is paused before a persisted implementation, with changed_files absent or equivalent no-diff evidence and branches differing in core Text tracing versus downstream MathText investigation. Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a continuation that identifies the causal chain from Text.__init__ or _reset_visual_defaults, through a stored antialiasing value and getter/setter, into Text.draw setting the GraphicsContext, then to backend consumers reading GraphicsContext state. Also credit locating update_from and Annotation behavior, recognizing the existing rcParams value as the fallback, and using analogous artist implementations to guide the design. A visible source inspection or persisted edit is stronger than a prose plan, but at this paused stage it remains exploration unless the final state visibly contains the edit. Contradictory evidence: Do not rank MathText parser or rasterization searches above a continuation that establishes the core Text state contract. Do not treat a backend-only grep, a generic dependency setup, or a script's success message as proof that the feature is implemented. Do not infer that a missing backend edit is a final implementation defect when no persisted patch exists at all. Close-looking exclusions: Reading MathText after first locating the Text-to-GraphicsContext path is not contradictory; score the core causal connection first. Inspecting Line2D or Patch is relevant evidence rather than unrelated exploration. Import or dependency failures do not disprove the diagnosis. Annotation need not have bespoke methods if ordinary inheritance demonstrably preserves the state, and MathText need not be edited in a particular file if the same GraphicsContext state is correctly honored through its actual rendering path. Accept equivalent fallback placement, accessor implementation, state-copying mechanism, and safe edit method when the observable semantics are the same. Explicitly rejected misleading direction or weighting: Reject any rubric that gives greater weight to continued downstream MathText exploration merely because it is technically detailed, while ignoring the required Text state and draw-time handoff. Reject any rubric that awards implementation-completeness penalties or full backend credit from command intent alone when the visible summary shows no persisted diff. Backend discovery is a useful completeness discriminator, but it must not outweigh the first-order per-artist state contract at this stage. Abstention boundary: If all visible branches show only listing, generic searches, or environment setup and none connects Text state to GraphicsContext behavior, keep them tied or abstain from diagnosis ranking. If source output is truncated or the final persistence status is unclear, do not classify the change as implemented or broken. Do not require passing rendering tests before a patch is visible, and do not predict eventual backend or MathText correctness from exploration order alone.

experiences.title: Rank kbd separator fixes by rendered semantics, not tokenizer style
experiences.description: For :kbd: fixes where -, +, or ^ can be either compound separators or literal keystrokes, prioritize visible output semantics and preserve equivalent implementations rather than rewarding a particular parsing strategy.
experiences.context: The visible task concerns malformed nested kbd elements for standalone separators and compounds such as Shift-+. Candidate changes use different control flows, including indexed iteration and split-based parsing. The judge view includes both custom parser checks and actual Sphinx-generated HTML checks, so the user-visible behavior is directly distinguishable.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when ranking continuations for the kbd separator bug and the visible view contains candidate source changes plus any parser, docutils-node, or rendered-HTML validation.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a continuation whose visible post-edit Sphinx output or docutils structure shows standalone -, +, and ^ as literal non-empty kbd content; Shift-+ as Shift, separator -, and literal +; ordinary chords such as Ctrl+Shift+A preserved; and no empty nested kbd elements. A visible assertion over the generated structure is strong evidence even if the implementation uses regex splitting, index arithmetic, or another equivalent method.

Contradictory evidence: Actual output containing empty nested kbd elements, dropped separators, treating the literal + in Shift-+ as a separator, or breaking ordinary compound chords is decisive negative evidence. A custom splitter prototype, source diff, patch file, or claim that tests passed without visible rendered or node-structure results is only partial evidence and must not outrank a branch with direct successful output.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not require character-by-character parsing, positional parity, or any other particular algorithm. Do not automatically penalize split-based code when its visible output satisfies all required cases, and do not automatically reward a more elaborate tokenizer. Do not award separate weight for the quantity of manual test commands, narration quality, patch-submission mechanics, or investigation of unrelated pre-existing failures. A generic suite pass is weaker than a focused rendered check, while an unrelated footnote failure does not disprove the kbd behavior. Equivalent implementations with equivalent visible semantic coverage should tie.

Abstention boundary: If no visible output or node structure exercises the affected cases, do not infer correctness from the diff, algorithm description, prototype-only results, or successful build setup. If output is truncated so that the relevant kbd contents cannot be inspected, preserve uncertainty. If only some cases are visible, credit only those cases and do not extrapolate to the unobserved separator or compound forms.

Explicit rubric correction: Reject the observed misleading direction that heavily favors character-by-character or context-aware tokenizer style over split-based implementations, and reject weighting generic regression-failure investigation as a primary discriminator. The decisive criterion is demonstrated preservation of literal-key and separator semantics in the generated structure.

experiences.title: Rank Causal Field-Preparation Reruns Above Isolated Lazy-Wrapper Introspection
experiences.description: For the nested-subquery SimpleLazyObject regression, prefer a visible field-preparation edit followed by the original reproduction over toy inspection of _wrapped, empty, _setup(), or class hierarchies. A changed failure from the wrapper to its underlying model instance proves partial causal progress, not completion.
experiences.context: The visible failure occurs when lookup preparation sends a SimpleLazyObject toward numeric field coercion. The base Field.get_prep_value() visibly handles Promise values but not LazyObject values, while ForeignKey preparation delegates to its target field. Some continuations only inspect LazyObject internals. Others import LazyObject, add unwrapping to Field.get_prep_value(), and rerun the same reproduction. Those reruns no longer report the SimpleLazyObject as the offending value; they report the underlying User object, showing that the wrapper was traversed but that relation/model-instance normalization is still unresolved. The visible toy checks also establish that a fresh wrapper's _wrapped attribute can still be the empty sentinel.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply when ranking work on a SimpleLazyObject or LazyObject failure during ORM lookup/field preparation, especially when the traceback reaches Field.get_prep_value(), IntegerField coercion, ForeignKey delegation, or a nested Subquery annotation, and the trajectories differ between internal wrapper inspection and an applied source edit with a rerun.

Decisive positive evidence: The strongest evidence is a visible source change at Field.get_prep_value() or an equivalent appropriate preparation boundary, followed by execution of the same nested-subquery scenario. Full validation requires the filter to compile or evaluate successfully and exhibit the expected queryset behavior. Before that point, explicitly credit a rerun whose error changes from a SimpleLazyObject complaint to a complaint about the underlying model instance: this demonstrates that the edited path actually traversed the lazy wrapper. Among incomplete edits, prefer mechanisms that safely initialize an unevaluated wrapper, such as checking the empty sentinel before setup or using an established reduction-style mechanism already visible elsewhere in the code, over unconditional _wrapped access. Preserve any equivalent implementation that safely resolves the lazy value at the proper preparation boundary, retains existing Promise behavior, and allows normal relation or primary-key preparation to continue.

Contradictory evidence: A User-to-integer TypeError is not a successful fix. It proves unwrapping for that run but also proves that the underlying model instance still reaches numeric coercion incorrectly. If the original SimpleLazyObject TypeError remains unchanged after an edit, no causal improvement is shown. Unconditionally returning value._wrapped is suspect when a fresh wrapper visibly contains the empty sentinel; success after earlier printing or other access may only reflect accidental prior evaluation. A run that stops at an import, dependency, settings, or collection failure provides no behavioral evidence about the edit.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not treat MRO output, identification of the Promise/LazyObject hierarchy gap, inspection of _wrapped and _setup(), or discovery of the empty sentinel as equivalent to changing source and rerunning the failing query. Printing a lazy object before inspecting _wrapped can itself force evaluation, so an evaluated toy example does not establish safe handling of a fresh wrapper. Searching for force-string helpers does not validate model-instance or foreign-key preparation. Conversely, do not demand one exact private helper or patch shape: setup plus wrapped-value access, a reduction-based approach, or another safe mechanism may be equivalent. A changed exception is meaningful partial evidence but must never be relabeled as end-to-end success.

Misleading rubric direction or weighting to reject: Reject the observed rubric that awards its highest diagnosis score for increasingly detailed practical exploration of _wrapped, empty, _setup(), and the class hierarchy. That weighting incorrectly places clean helper-level introspection above a causally relevant source edit with observable before/after behavior. Applied progress should rank higher, while still receiving only partial credit until the underlying model instance is prepared to the correct database value and the target query succeeds.

Abstention boundary: If no trajectory visibly applies a relevant source edit and reruns the reported path, abstain from claims about fix correctness and compare only diagnosis quality. If a rerun is truncated before lookup preparation is reached, withhold behavioral credit. If all applied edits merely change the exception to a model-instance coercion failure, keep them in the incomplete-fix tier and distinguish them only by visibly supported safety of their unwrapping mechanism; do not infer eventual success.

experiences.title: For Prompt-Supplied Parser Symptoms, Rank Source-and-Regression Readiness Above Reproduction Setup
experiences.description: At a paused, pre-edit parser task where the prompt already provides an exact failing example, successful re-reproduction after dependency work should not dominate ranking. Prefer continuations that inspect the complete conversion path and existing regression-test structure, while abstaining from parser-versus-printer conclusions unsupported by structural evidence.
experiences.context: Use when continuations for a missing-parentheses or precedence report have no visible source patch and differ mainly in dependency setup, repetition of the supplied reproduction, inspection of the relevant conversion function, and inspection of existing tests. The visible nested-fraction case points to convert_frac and requires preserving simple fractions, but the paused evidence does not yet prove whether conversion or rendering ultimately needs modification.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply when the task prompt already states the exact input, wrong output, expected output, and compatibility constraint; all compared continuations are paused before a visible source edit; and the visible work ranges from dependency troubleshooting or reproduction to inspection of the relevant conversion body and test suite.

Decisive positive evidence: Give strongest pre-implementation credit to a continuation that displays the complete relevant function body, identifies the exact construction boundary—conversion of numerator and denominator followed by inverse Pow and outer Mul—and inspects the existing fraction tests or their non-evaluating helper conventions. A concrete regression plan covering the reported nested denominator and existing simple cases is stronger still. An attempted structural probe using srepr, args, or structural equality is useful diagnostic preparation even if execution is blocked, but it is not mandatory merely to recognize implementation readiness at this paused stage.

Contradictory evidence: Repeated package installation, editable-install attempts, generated-lexer inspection, or import failures do not diagnose the fraction behavior. Resolving the runtime incompatibility and printing exactly the mismatch already present in the prompt confirms that execution is possible, but does not by itself identify the faulty layer or prepare a regression. A grep that only finds the convert_frac name is weaker than output showing its body. With no source diff, do not describe any continuation as having committed to parser surgery, inversion tricks, or a printer fix.

Close-looking exclusions: Diagnosing the runtime-version mismatch is useful environment work, but it is not the root cause of the nested-fraction behavior. A failed local reproduction does not erase direct source and test inspection. Conversely, a clean reproduction does not outrank such inspection merely because it executed. Distinguish viewing the active conversion body and test assertions from broad cat/grep commands whose relevant output is absent. Structural inspection can later determine parser versus printer responsibility, but speculation that the AST is flat or that the printer is ambiguous is not evidence for either conclusion.

Explicitly rejected misleading direction and weighting: Reject making successful reproduction the highest-weight criterion when the prompt already supplies the complete symptom. Also reject a mechanism rubric that treats the visible Pow/Mul lines as proof that the AST loses grouping. Equally reject the supplied printer-first audit direction as a basis for ranking these prefixes: no visible continuation inspected the printer or established a correct AST, and no continuation made the parser rewrite that the audit claims. Do not require a printer-side repair, a convert_frac repair, a grammar change, or any particular constructor pattern without later evidence. Preserve equivalent valid implementations that satisfy structural or behavioral regressions and retain simple-fraction behavior.

Abstention boundary: If the question is which layer must ultimately be changed, abstain until visible structural output, a focused patch, or regression results distinguish conversion structure from rendering. If all continuations show only setup failures or superficial searches, abstain from ranking their implementation prospects. This abstention does not prevent ranking visible pre-implementation progress: complete conversion-path and regression-test inspection is observably more actionable than merely repeating a prompt-supplied output.

experiences.title: Do not rank Bareiss fixes by deletion minimality when intermediate cancellation can be preserved
experiences.description: Use this experience when visible Matrix.det trajectories differ in how they handle the non-atomic Bareiss entry calculation: leaving cancel(ret) as a bare call, assigning its returned value to ret, deleting the intermediate cancellation, or changing the generic exprtools NaN comparison. The judge must distinguish a direct algorithm edit from symptom suppression and must not assume that the smallest deletion is automatically the correct implementation.
experiences.context: In the symbolic determinant task, the Bareiss entry function computes ret and conditionally calls cancel(ret), while the outer determinant computation also performs a final cancellation. The visible traceback shows that the intermediate call reaches factor_terms and raises Invalid NaN comparison. A branch that changes the call to ret = cancel(ret) preserves the intended per-entry normalization and uses the function's returned expression. A branch that deletes the block may avoid the immediate exception, but its equivalence is not established merely by observing that a final cancellation exists. Changes to exprtools.py alter a generic simplification path and are a symptom-level alternative rather than evidence of a better determinant fix.
experiences.experience: Activation conditions: Apply when the paused view exposes the Bareiss entry code and at least two branches visibly differ between assigning cancel's result, deleting the cancellation block, modifying exprtools.py, or making only environment fixes. Positive evidence: Prefer a direct target-function edit that changes the ineffective `cancel(ret)` call to `ret = cancel(ret)` while retaining the non-atomic guard, because it both eliminates the observed no-op and preserves intermediate normalization.
