experiences.description: For the paused matplotlib clear() regression, a label-only diagnosis is incomplete even when it finds the exact tick-keyword dictionary clear. Rank higher only visible investigation that distinguishes label1On/label2On from tick1On/tick2On and checks the rcParams-to-tick_params initialization or translation path needed to explain the independent top/right tick-mark symptom.
experiences.context: Apply to pre-patch investigation of ax.clear() causing hidden shared-subplot labels and normally absent top/right tick marks to reappear. Relevant visible code includes Axes initialization and cla(), Axis.clear(), the major/minor tick-keyword resets, set_tick_params translation, and SubplotBase outer-label methods. All visible continuations are paused without source edits, so this rule evaluates diagnosis direction rather than completed implementation.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply only when the visible task reports both shared-subplot label leakage after clear() and top/right tick marks appearing even without shared subplots, and the continuations are inspecting the axis-clear and tick-parameter lifecycle.

Hard discriminator: Treat the distinction between tick-label visibility and tick-mark visibility as a gate, not an optional bonus. A continuation that explains only how _label_outer_xaxis() or _label_outer_yaxis() stores hidden-label policy as label1On/label2On, and how Axis.clear removes those keys, must remain below a continuation that visibly investigates the separate side-tick state. Naming _reset_major_tick_kw(), _reset_minor_tick_kw(), their clear operations, and the cla() call chain is useful localization but is not a complete causal diagnosis.

Decisive positive evidence: Strong evidence follows both halves of the lifecycle. For shared labels, it connects outer-label calls such as labelbottom=False, labeltop=False, labelleft=False, or labelright=False to translated label1On/label2On state in the major and minor tick dictionaries. For the independent top/right marks, it inspects the Axes initialization block that applies rcParams-derived side defaults through tick_params, or examines how set_tick_params translates bottom/top or left/right controls into tick1On/tick2On. It then recognizes that clearing the dictionaries erases both classes of translated state; creating ticks without the initialization-applied side settings can therefore restore constructor-side behavior that includes unwanted second-side marks. Actual inspection of the initialization or translation code is strongest. Deliberately moving from the reset site to that code is positive directional evidence at a pause, but is weaker until the distinct mappings are observed or articulated.

Contradictory evidence: A statement that erased label1On/label2On fully explains the bug contradicts the reported non-shared top/right tick marks. Reapplying label_outer alone addresses subplot label policy but does not by itself explain or correct a single ordinary axis gaining top/right tick marks. Likewise, blanket preservation of every major and minor tick keyword across clear() is not established as sound: Axis.clear visibly promises to reset axis properties, so preserving unrelated user styling requires justification. Claims that sharex/sharey linkage was destroyed also conflict with the report that range linkage still works.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not confuse top/right tick marks with top/right tick labels; their public options translate to separate tick1On/tick2On and label1On/label2On state. Do not award complete-mechanism credit for a grep that merely finds label1On, label2On, or the dictionary clear. Reading outer-label call sites is relevant to the shared-label symptom but not the non-shared symptom. Reading the rcParams tick_params initialization without connecting it to the later reset is also partial. History searches and failed local build or reproduction attempts are neutral unless they lead to the relevant active-source semantics.

Equivalent valid implementations: Preserve any eventual approach that restores the intended side defaults and shared-subplot label policy while keeping axis linkage and appropriate clear semantics. Targeted state preservation, reconstruction of the initialization baseline, safe policy reapplication, or another behaviorally equivalent design may all be valid. Do not demand one patch location or exact code shape from pre-patch evidence.

Explicitly rejected misleading bias: Reject the rubric that gives highest diagnosis credit merely for identifying _major_tick_kw.clear(), label1On/label2On, and the cla() to Axis.clear chain. That rubric rewards an exact token-level path whose causal account fails the task's independent non-shared tick-mark symptom. Also reject eloquent declarations that label_outer should simply be called again when the continuation has not examined tick-side defaults or translation.

Abstention boundary: If no continuation visibly inspects or deliberately pursues the rcParams side-default setup, set_tick_params translation, tick1On/tick2On state, or the non-shared symptom, keep label-only continuations close or tied rather than predicting implementation success. If several continuations equally distinguish both state classes and connect initialization to reset, do not break the tie using command volume, history depth, or reproduction setup. No patch means final correctness and side-effect safety remain unknown.

experiences.title: Split a typed docfield at the final name boundary, not every whitespace occurrence
experiences.description: For `:param type name:` parsing, the decisive defect is the later split that treats the first whitespace inside `dict(str, str) opc_meta` as the type/name boundary. The parameter name is the final token, so a right-biased whitespace split is the direct, minimal correction. Do not reward changing every similar-looking split, implementing delimiter grammar, or removing exception handling unless visible evidence shows those changes are necessary and contract-preserving.
experiences.context: The visible source performs two different operations. The earlier `field_name.astext().split(None, 1)` separates a field marker such as `param` from its complete argument. The later `fieldarg.split(None, 1)` separates an inline type from the parameter name and visibly misparses `dict(str, str) opc_meta` as `dict(str,` plus `str) opc_meta`. A construct such as `fieldarg.rsplit(None, 1)` directly preserves the complete type and extracts `opc_meta`.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply this rule when evaluating a paused fix for typed docfields and the visible source or reproduction shows that the type may contain whitespace while the parameter name is the final token.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a focused change to the later typed-field split that extracts the final name, such as `fieldarg.rsplit(None, 1)`, while preserving the existing no-separator behavior. Visible output mapping `dict(str, str) opc_meta` to `('dict(str, str)', 'opc_meta')` confirms the core parsing mechanism. Keeping the earlier field-marker split unchanged is strong scope evidence. An alternative nesting-aware implementation remains valid if visible tests demonstrate the same final-name contract, normal whitespace handling, and no unrelated parsing changes.

Contradictory evidence: Leaving the later split unchanged preserves the demonstrated bug. Editing only Napoleon, cross-reference punctuation splitting, or rendering code does not correct the visibly wrong type/name pair. Reusing a right-biased helper for the earlier field-marker split would be incorrect because that stage must extract the first token, `param`, rather than the final token. Changing both sites is not completeness evidence merely because both contain `split(None, 1)`.

Close-looking exclusions: Reject the observed “fix all occurrences” bias: the two splits have different semantic roles, so textual similarity does not make both vulnerable. Reject bracket-coverage scoring as a requirement: a right-biased split handles the reported type without recognizing parentheses, square brackets, or braces at all. Reject unconditional credit for removing the surrounding `try/except`: `rsplit(None, 1)` still raises when no separator exists, and an alternative non-raising helper must preserve that fallback through equivalent control flow. Also do not blame punctuation splitting used later to construct type cross-references; that occurs after the incorrect type/name extraction and does not explain the swapped or truncated parameter text.

Abstention boundary: If no continuation visibly shows the failing parse, a corrected parse, or the relevant typed-field source change, do not infer correctness from file exploration or dependency setup. If two implementations both visibly preserve the final-name contract, whitespace behavior, fallback behavior, and focused scope, do not prefer one solely because it uses `rsplit` or a differently named helper. Without rendered-output validation, treat parser-level success as strong directional evidence rather than complete end-to-end confirmation.

Co-retrieval application rule: Apply this task-specific experience only when its visible problem and trajectory evidence match. When it matches, do not let generic or unrelated co-retrieved experiences replace its concrete semantic boundary. Generate at least one high-weight rubric that directly tests the criteria below, and score every continuation against the same visible-evidence standard.

Required task-specific rubric semantics:
Criterion: Focused Fix Scope: Correctly Targets Only the Later Typed-Field Split
Meaning: Evaluates whether the fix correctly identifies and modifies only the later split operation (around line 301) that separates the inline type from the parameter name, while leaving the earlier field-marker split (around line 241) unchanged. The earlier split extracts the field marker (e.g., 'param') from the complete argument and must use left-biased splitting. The later split extracts the parameter name (the final token) from the type+name string and is the actual source of the bug. A correct fix modifies only the later split. Additionally, the fix should use a minimal approach (e.g., rsplit(None, 1) or equivalent right-biased split) rather than implementing unnecessary nesting-aware bracket tracking, since the parameter name is simply the final whitespace-delimited token.
Critical boundary: The two split(None, 1) calls have different semantic roles: earlier extracts first token (field marker), later extracts last token (parameter name). Only the later one is buggy.
Judge focus: Whether the fix modifies only the later split (line ~301) and not the earlier field-marker split (line ~241); whether the fix uses minimal right-biased splitting rather than complex nesting-aware logic

Criterion: End-to-End Validation of Docfield Rendering Fix
Meaning: Evaluates whether the continuation validates the fix through actual Sphinx documentation rendering rather than only unit-level parsing tests. For a rendering bug where :param dict(str, str) opc_meta: displays incorrectly, the gold-standard validation is building actual Sphinx documentation and inspecting the rendered HTML output to confirm the parameter name and full type render correctly as a coherent unit. Strong evidence includes: creating a minimal test project with the exact bug syntax, running sphinx-build to generate HTML, and verifying the HTML shows 'opc_meta (dict(str, str))' rendered correctly rather than fragmented or truncated. Weak evidence includes only standalone Python function tests or pytest runs without checking the actual rendered HTML output that users see.
Critical boundary: Parsing correctness does not guarantee rendering correctness; the full docfield pipeline must be exercised
Judge focus: Whether the continuation performs end-to-end Sphinx build validation with HTML inspection, not just unit-level parsing tests

Criterion: Fix Implementation Completeness
Meaning: Evaluates whether the continuation has progressed beyond diagnosis to actually implement and apply a fix to the source code. A complete implementation includes: (1) identifying the buggy split operation in sphinx/util/docfields.py, (2) creating a helper function or inline fix to correctly parse type annotations with spaces, (3) applying the fix to the source file via sed, patch, or Python script, and (4) verifying the modified source code reflects the change. Continuations that only explore the codebase, identify the bug location, or test parsing logic in isolation without modifying the actual source file have not completed the fix implementation.
Critical boundary: File exploration and bug identification are necessary but insufficient; the source code must be modified
Judge focus: Whether the continuation has actually modified sphinx/util/docfields.py with a fix, not just diagnosed the bug

Criterion: Error Handling Contract Preservation
Meaning: Evaluates whether the fix preserves the original error handling contract around the typed-field split operation. The original code wraps the split in a try/except ValueError block to handle cases where no whitespace separator exists (e.g., a fieldarg with only a type and no parameter name). A correct fix must preserve this fallback behavior: if the new split operation can still raise ValueError when no separator exists, the try/except must be retained. If the new helper function never raises ValueError, the try/except may be removed but equivalent fallback logic must exist. Removing the try/except without ensuring the replacement cannot raise ValueError is a contract violation that could cause crashes on edge cases.
Critical boundary: The original try/except exists for a reason - fieldarg may have no separator
Judge focus: Whether the fix preserves ValueError handling for cases where fieldarg has no whitespace separator

experiences.title: Use a conjunctive semantic-and-fix gate when ranking paused SpanSelector initialization work
experiences.description: For the interactive SpanSelector axes-limit bug, do not independently award several high-weight scores for source-path inspection, rectangle geometry, and repetition of the same causal chain. Top pre-patch progress requires both correct construction-time semantics and a concrete, lifecycle-safe initialization direction. A complete diagnosis without a proposed initialization change remains below a continuation that has the same diagnosis and has begun designing such a change.
experiences.context: During SpanSelector initialization, new_axes creates a Rectangle at (0, 0) using a blended transform. The Rectangle spans the orthogonal axes dimension, but has zero size along the selected data axis, so self.extents is initially (0, 0). Interactive setup passes those extents to ToolLineHandles, whose constructor creates axvline or axhline artists at zero. Several paused continuations can discover this same chain without yet editing source. Their useful distinction is whether they correctly preserve these semantics and then move toward preventing the initial handle artists from introducing an out-of-view coordinate while retaining later interactive behavior.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply at a pre-patch pause for the interactive SpanSelector limit-expansion bug when multiple continuations have inspected new_axes, _setup_edge_handle, self.extents, or ToolLineHandles and at least one continuation has begun discussing how initialization should change.

Highest-weight conjunctive discriminator: Reserve the top tier for visible reasoning that contains both parts. First, it must correctly state the construction-time semantics: the Rectangle spans the orthogonal axis through a blended transform but has zero extent along the selector axis, so the horizontal or vertical selector reports selector-axis extents (0, 0); _setup_edge_handle passes those positions to the ToolLineHandles constructor; and that constructor creates axvline(0) or axhline(0), introducing coordinate zero during artist registration and autoscaling. Second, it must translate that diagnosis into a concrete initialization-site direction that avoids introducing an out-of-range handle coordinate while preserving later handle updates and dragging. A continuation satisfying only the first part should be capped at diagnosis-level progress.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a continuation that localizes the change to SpanSelector initialization or the handle-construction boundary and proposes an actionable semantic strategy. Examples include choosing an initial handle position guaranteed to lie within the current selected-axis view, creating or registering the handles without allowing their placeholder position to alter the existing limits, or deferring meaningful placement until selector extents exist while still ensuring the handles are subsequently created and updated. Equivalent implementations are valid. The essential invariant is that construction preserves the preexisting limits and later self.extents updates continue to move functional interactive handles. Even before exact code is written, an explicit proposal to replace the zero placeholder with an in-view initialization is stronger than another recital of the cause.

Contradictory evidence: Treat an assertion that ToolLineHandles.closest causes construction-time autoscaling as incorrect. Its transData transformations containing (p, 0) or (0, p) calculate interaction-time distances; they do not create the initial artists. Also treat it as a semantic error to infer selector-axis extents of (0, 1) merely because the Rectangle spans the orthogonal axis. For a horizontal selector, width is zero along x while height spans the axes; for a vertical selector, height is zero along y while width spans the axes. Removing the handles, preventing later set_data updates, or otherwise sacrificing interactive dragging contradicts the task contract. Failed imports, editable-install failures, and reproduction scripts that never execute provide no validation of a proposed fix.

Close-looking exclusions: Reading new_axes, extents, ToolLineHandles, and axvline/axhline may all support one causal diagnosis, but they are not four independent achievements and must not be additively weighted until they overwhelm implementation-directed reasoning. Asking whether invisible or animated lines participate in autoscaling can confirm the mechanism, but it is not yet a fix strategy. Conversely, a proposal to use a different initial coordinate is meaningful directional evidence only when it is tied to the selected data axis and existing view; the phrase 'proper coordinates' by itself is too vague for top-tier credit. Saving and restoring limits, safe in-view initialization, and lifecycle-aware deferred placement should remain eligible rather than requiring one exact implementation.

Explicitly rejected misleading bias: Reject a rubric portfolio that separately gives substantial weight to targeted code-path reading, Rectangle geometry, and complete causal-chain wording when those criteria all measure the same diagnosis. That double- or triple-counting can rank a diagnosis-only continuation above one that has the same correct mechanism plus a concrete initialization fix direction. Also reject the bias that the most detailed repetition of 'Rectangle at zero to extents to axvline/axhline to autoscale' is automatically the best continuation. Once that chain is shared, the decisive visible evidence is whether the continuation begins a semantically valid change at initialization and preserves the interactive lifecycle.

Abstention boundary: If all visible continuations establish the same construction chain but none proposes or evaluates an initialization change, preserve a tie about implementation readiness. If no continuation correctly distinguishes selector-axis extents from the orthogonal axes-spanning dimension, use a diagnosis rubric rather than predicting implementation quality. If multiple continuations present equally concrete, contract-preserving strategies, do not choose among them without a visible change or behavioral evidence.

Co-retrieval application rule: Apply this task-specific experience only when its visible problem and trajectory evidence match. When it matches, do not let generic or unrelated co-retrieved experiences replace its concrete semantic boundary. Generate at least one high-weight rubric that directly tests the criteria below, and score every continuation against the same visible-evidence standard. Resolve conflicts explicitly: a continuation that crosses a listed critical boundary must outrank one that merely looks more complete, runs more commands, or produces broader but non-diagnostic validation.

Case-specific correction: Do not count dependency installation attempts as execution readiness unless they lead to an actual local reproduction of the reported ordering. Both compared paths identify zero-valued initial extents; prefer the concise path that directly proves _setup_edge_handle receives self.extents=(0,0) during construction. Penalize pip/install churn that still ends in import or extension errors and adds no target-behavior observation. Precise construction-order diagnosis must outrank unsuccessful environment work.

Required task-specific rubric semantics:
Criterion: Construction-Time Causal Diagnosis with Initialization Fix Direction
Meaning: Evaluates whether the continuation correctly identifies the construction-time causal chain (Rectangle at (0,0) → extents (0,0) → ToolLineHandles creates axvline/axhline at zero → autoscaling) AND proposes a concrete initialization-site strategy to prevent the out-of-view coordinate while preserving interactive lifecycle. Continuations that misattribute the cause to ToolLineHandles.closest (which only calculates interaction-time distances) or that only diagnose without proposing a fix direction score lower.
Judge focus: Whether the continuation correctly distinguishes construction-time artist creation (axvline/axhline in ToolLineHandles.__init__) from interaction-time distance calculation (ToolLineHandles.closest), and whether it proposes an actionable initialization strategy
Low score: No causal diagnosis or incorrect attribution (e.g., blames ToolLineHandles.closest transData transformations, which are interaction-time distance calculations, not construction-time artist creation); or only environment setup with no code-level analysis
High score: Complete diagnosis with lifecycle-aware fix strategy: correctly traces the full construction chain AND proposes a specific initialization change that preserves the interactive dragging lifecycle (e.g., safe in-view initialization, deferred placement with subsequent updates, or limit-save-restore at construction), with reasoning about why the strategy preserves later handle behavior

experiences.title: For mixed FiniteSet–Interval difference, require three-way membership partitioning rather than a blanket unevaluated fallback
experiences.description: Use when diagnosing a set difference containing both numeric and symbolic finite-set members. Correct progress must distinguish members known to be inside the interval, known to be outside it, and of indeterminate membership. Merely returning None for every mixed set preserves too much and does not produce the requested simplification.
experiences.context: For `Complement(FiniteSet(x, y, 2), Interval(-10, 10))`, dispatch reaches `Interval._complement(FiniteSet(...))`. The existing fallback removes elements whose containment is definitely true but also collapses unknown symbolic membership into a bare finite set. However, changing the mixed-case guard to return None is not a complete fix: it leaves the provably included `2` in the unevaluated left operand. The required result removes known-inside numbers while retaining unknown symbols under a Complement; a case such as `FiniteSet(x, 2, 15)` additionally requires retaining the known-outside `15`.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply when a paused SymPy trajectory is diagnosing or implementing mixed `FiniteSet` minus `Interval` behavior and the visible reasoning discusses the `Complement.reduce` dispatch, `Interval._complement`, the `nums == []` guard, or the base `Set._complement` filtering fallback.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer reasoning, tests, or edits that partition finite-set members by containment result. Members for which interval containment is definitely true must be removed; members for which it is definitely false must remain directly in the result; members whose containment is indeterminate must remain represented under an unevaluated Complement. For the reported case, this means removing `2` while preserving the unresolved difference involving `x` and `y`. A stronger probe such as `FiniteSet(x, 2, 15) - Interval(-10, 10)` demonstrates awareness that `2`, `15`, and `x` occupy three distinct categories. Credit any valid implementation location or equivalent result structure that preserves these semantics.

Decisive contradictory evidence: A proposal to return None solely because a finite set contains a mixture of symbols and numbers is incomplete. It prevents the incorrect bare `{x, y}` result, but it also leaves the known-inside `2` in the unevaluated minuend and therefore misses the requested simplification. Likewise, continuing through the current base fallback and returning bare `{x, y}` is wrong because it loses the unresolved relationship between each symbol and the interval. A precise trace of `Complement.reduce -> Interval._complement -> Set._complement` does not compensate for either semantic error.

Close-looking exclusions: Returning an entirely unevaluated original expression is mathematically conservative but does not satisfy this task's requirement to simplify membership that is already decidable. Returning a bare finite set is also not sufficient, because unknown symbolic membership cannot be treated as definitely outside. Do not require one exact source method or one printed normal form: an equivalent implementation may partition in `Interval._complement`, `FiniteSet._complement`, `Complement.reduce`, or another appropriate path, and known-outside members may appear in an equivalent union structure. Environment compatibility work is useful prerequisite progress but does not validate the set-operation semantics by itself.

Misleading rubric or judge bias to reject: Reject a rubric that awards top diagnosis credit for identifying the narrow `nums == []` condition and then declares that it should simply return None for every mixed case. That rubric confuses preventing premature evaluation with performing the required partial simplification. Also reject ranking polished causal prose above a branch that visibly states and probes the correct inside/outside/unknown partition.

Abstention boundary: If the visible prefix contains only method inspection or import failures and no branch states a proposed result for known-inside, known-outside, and unknown members, do not infer which implementation will be correct. If branches differ only in edit location while expressing equivalent three-way semantics, preserve equivalence until runtime or structural validation distinguishes them.

experiences.title: SpanSelector autoscale validation must preserve the reported pre-limit-query ordering
experiences.description: For the interactive SpanSelector limit regression, do not treat a direct Line2D/add_line change as proven merely because a custom script reports unchanged limits after first querying get_xlim or get_ylim. Querying limits before selector construction materializes pending autoscaling and changes the failure condition. Prefer visible fixes that prevent zero-valued handles from entering dataLim before the first limit calculation, while preserving the existing handle lifecycle.
experiences.context: The reported sequence is ax.plot(...), then SpanSelector(..., interactive=True), then display, with no intervening limit query. Paused continuations include a broad ToolLineHandles rewrite using Line2D/add_line and a localized _setup_edge_handle change that initializes handles from the current directional axis bounds. The broad rewrite has custom before/after scripts; the localized change has a visible target-file diff but runtime execution is blocked by dependencies.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when evaluating paused fixes for SpanSelector(interactive=True) expanding limits to include zero, especially when one implementation bypasses axvline/axhline with Line2D/add_line and another initializes the existing ToolLineHandles at current axis bounds.

Decisive positive evidence: The strongest visible approach prevents zero from participating in the first pending autoscale calculation. A localized `_setup_edge_handle` change that obtains `ax.get_xlim()` for horizontal selection or `ax.get_ylim()` for vertical selection and passes those positions to the existing `ToolLineHandles` is positive evidence: the limit query materializes the plotted-data bounds, the initial lines are placed within those bounds, and later `extents` updates continue using the established `set_data` lifecycle. It also retains existing direction changes, line properties, unit handling, visibility, removal, and closest-handle behavior. A different implementation remains valid if it visibly prevents initial handle coordinates from contaminating `dataLim` and succeeds under the exact reported ordering.

Decisive contradictory evidence: Merely replacing `axvline`/`axhline` with `Line2D` followed by `ax.add_line` is not sufficient. The visible `add_line` path invokes `_update_line_limits`; adding handles at the initial zero positions can therefore place zero in `dataLim`. If autoscaling from the preceding plot is still pending, the first later limit calculation or draw can include zero even though the explicit `_request_autoscale_view` call was bypassed. Custom output is not decisive when the script calls `get_xlim()` or `get_ylim()` before constructing SpanSelector, because that pre-query resolves pending autoscaling and tests a materially easier ordering than the report.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not confuse “before/after limits were equal” with reproduction fidelity; inspect where the “before” value was obtained. The exact regression test must construct the selector immediately after plotting and only then inspect limits. Do not assume direct Line2D construction is invalid in every form—credit it if visible code addresses data-limit mutation or exact-order execution proves the reported contract. Do not reject the localized current-limit approach as a mere workaround solely because it retains axvline/axhline; positions already inside the materialized bounds do not request expansion and preserve more existing behavior. An earlier malformed patch application is not a current contradiction after the file is visibly restored and a corrected git diff is shown. At a paused pre-submission state, absence of patch.txt is not evidence that a semantically stronger visible edit is wrong.

Misleading rubric/judge bias to reject: Reject the rubric preference that labels direct Line2D construction the unique root-cause solution and awards it high confidence from custom test volume. That preference overlooks `add_line` data-limit updates and the fact that pre-reading limits changes the reported execution order. Also reject ranking a dependency-blocked but semantically localized edit below such a misleading custom-test result merely because it has not yet produced a final patch artifact.

Abstention boundary: Abstain if the visible test script is truncated before the ordering of plot, limit query, and selector construction can be established, or if the proposed initialization positions and resulting add_line/axvline path are not visible. If every continuation only identifies zero-valued handles without showing an edit or an executable ordering, preserve uncertainty. Require future evidence when a direct-Line2D variant visibly avoids data-limit mutation but no exact-order result is available.

experiences.title: Concrete categorical-reference behavior outranks speculative Nominal bookkeeping during pre-patch diagnosis
experiences.description: When all continuations are paused before editing the target code for the Nominal-scale categorical-parity task, rank visible behavioral evidence and integration reasoning above isolated discovery of an internal category-count attribute or test-script volume. A continuation that visibly confirms the existing categorical contract and maps it to the Nominal finalization path is more promising than one that only speculates about _legend or units_seed without reaching the target behavior.
experiences.context: The task requires Nominal scales, including inferred ones, to use categorical-style limits at half a tick beyond the endpoints, suppress the nominal-axis grid while respecting the user/theme contract, and invert a nominal y-axis. The visible code contains the categorical reference in categorical.py, a Plotter._finalize_figure limit loop, axis-to-scale metadata, and Nominal scale setup with units_seed/_legend. The visible continuations are all pre-patch and some are blocked by a pandas compatibility error.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Use this rule when every visible branch has zero correct target-file edits and the judge must rank diagnosis or design progress rather than completed implementation.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a branch that visibly runs or otherwise reports the categorical reference behavior: tick-based category count, limits of -0.5 and n-0.5, grid suppression on the categorical axis, and reversed y limits for a categorical y-axis. Also credit a branch that connects those observations to the actual integration points: sub[axis], the relevant scale in the Plotter, Nominal detection, and the scale's category data, while recognizing that explicit user/theme grid overrides need deliberate handling. Identifying _legend[0] or units_seed is useful supporting evidence only when it is connected to the finalization logic and the expected limit formula. A branch that resolves an environment barrier and then examines the relevant source path is stronger than one that only installs versions, but it still remains below a branch with concrete behavioral evidence.

Contradictory evidence: Do not rank a branch highest merely because it found the precise-looking _legend[0] category-count mechanism, wrote a backup, or produced many scripts. An internal attribute observation without a working reproduction, integration reasoning, or patch is incomplete. Repeated dependency/version attempts that do not reach the task behavior, or a destructive source edit used to bypass the pandas option error that creates an indentation failure and must be reverted, are negative diagnostic signals. Empty, truncated, or failed Nominal runs do not establish correct limits, grid state, or inversion.

Close-looking exclusions: No patch is not itself a failure when all branches are paused pre-implementation; do not collapse every branch to the same floor. Conversely, creating a reproduction file, instantiating Nominal(), reading _legend, or inspecting the old categorical code in isolation is not equivalent to demonstrating Nominal behavior. A successful old categorical API observation is reference-contract evidence, not proof that Nominal already works. Do not require one particular implementation location: _finalize_figure, scale initialization, or another equivalent integration point may be valid, and sticky-edge/margin handling may be equivalent to direct limit handling when it preserves the contract.

Abstention boundary: If no branch visibly reaches the categorical reference behavior, identifies the relevant Nominal integration path, or produces a trustworthy reproduction result, preserve uncertainty and do not use command count or the apparent precision of an untested attribute hypothesis as a tiebreaker. If all outputs are truncated or environment-blocked, credit only visible source-level connections and keep implementation quality, regression safety, and user/theme override behavior unresolved until future evidence appears.

Rejected misleading bias: Explicitly reject the judge bias that treats isolated category-count discovery, dependency activity, backup creation, or exploration volume as superior to concrete behavioral evidence. The measured branch ranking must not elevate speculative _legend analysis over a continuation that visibly established the categorical contract and investigated how to apply it to Nominal scales.

experiences.title: Mpmath Rational Submission Ranking: Prefer Explicit Exact Operands Over Fraction-String Elegance
experiences.description: For the mpmath lambdify Rational fix, rank a module-formatted _print_Rational that converts e.p and e.q separately before division above a quoted-fraction shortcut whose broader parser compatibility is not demonstrated. Do not reward formatting elegance, dead denominator-one handling, or custom-test volume over the direct precision-preserving printer contract.
experiences.context: At the implementation and submission stage, continuations add _print_Rational to MpmathPrinter and visibly emit either mpf(p)/mpf(q) or mpf('p/q'). Both can appear to work in the installed environment, but explicit conversion of the integer numerator and denominator avoids native Python division without depending on a fraction-string grammar. The visible lambdify namespace imports mpmath names unqualified, making self._module_format('mpmath.mpf') necessary.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply when ranking submitted or nearly submitted fixes for the mpmath lambdify Rational issue and the visible implementations differ between separately wrapped numerator/denominator operands and a single quoted fraction passed to mpf.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a narrowly scoped _print_Rational in MpmathPrinter that accesses e.p and e.q, obtains the constructor through self._module_format('mpmath.mpf'), and emits exact operands before division, such as mpf(232)/mpf(3). This guarantees that native Python floating-point division does not occur before mpmath receives the values. Equivalent formatting implementations should receive equal implementation credit when they separately construct exact mpmath operands and preserve module qualification behavior. Generated source showing this form, followed by the reported nsolve result at full precision, is strong behavioral confirmation.

Decisive contradictory evidence: Plain p/q remains the original bug. An unquoted mpf(p/q) is also wrong because Python performs p/q before calling mpf. A literal mpmath.mpf reference is contradictory when execution visibly raises NameError under lambdify's unqualified namespace; it must be replaced with self._module_format usage or an equivalent namespace-aware mechanism. A quoted mpf('p/q') may execute in the installed environment, but it relies on fraction-string parsing rather than the direct e.p/e.q conversion contract. Without broader compatibility evidence, it should not outrank the explicit two-operand implementation merely because it is shorter.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not award extra implementation quality for q == 1 handling inside _print_Rational when visible dispatch analysis shows canonical integers are handled by _print_Integer before that method is reached. Do not penalize mpf(p)/mpf(q) for creating two constructor calls; operation count and generated-code brevity are not the task invariant. Method placement immediately after _print_Float versus later within MpmathPrinter is immaterial if dispatch and scope are correct. A temporary literal-namespace or unquoted-division error should not remain contradictory after a visible correction and successful rerun. Custom negative, large-denominator, and mixed-expression checks are useful validation, but their quantity does not make a parser-dependent implementation superior to the direct exact-operand form.

Misleading rubric or judge-bias rejection: Explicitly reject the elegance-first rubric that declares mpf('p/q') superior because it uses one constructor and fewer Python-level operations. The decisive requirement is robust precision-safe Rational emission through the mpmath printer, not minimal generated syntax. Also reject rewarding denominator-one special casing as a sophistication signal when normal printer dispatch makes that branch irrelevant for canonical integers. Rank the direct module-formatted e.p/e.q implementation first; use visible precision and regression tests to distinguish otherwise equivalent implementations.

Abstention boundary: If the visible state does not show the _print_Rational body or generated source, do not infer whether native division occurs. If only a quoted-fraction implementation is visible and it executes successfully, credit it as locally functional but abstain from claiming broad compatibility. If two branches both emit separately wrapped exact operands and neither has contradictory execution, treat their implementation quality as equivalent and distinguish them only using visible validation or submission evidence.

experiences.title: For draggable-figure pickling, rank executable round-trip progress above static serialization maximalism
experiences.description: When multiple continuations have plausible fixes for draggable legend and annotation pickling, do not rank them by counting `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` methods, removed attributes, or callback operations. Prefer the branch that preserves a plausible target patch and demonstrably advances the modified checkout toward an actual pickle round trip. A syntax-only shared-base implementation remains unverified, especially when its unpickle-time reconstruction and callback behavior have not been exercised.
experiences.context: The visible failure is caused by draggable helper state retaining a backend canvas. Plausible designs include removing transient draggable state at the Legend and Annotation owners or teaching the shared DraggableBase path to omit and possibly reconstruct backend state. In the paused continuations, multiple such patches look structurally plausible. The meaningful distinction is that one continuation syntax-checks the target file, successfully builds the local extensions, and runs the reproduction far enough to expose only a missing `pyparsing` dependency, while others stop after static inspection, syntax checking, or an unexecuted submission.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions:
- Apply to the draggable legend or draggable annotation pickle failure after the canvas-retention mechanism has already been localized.
- Apply when two or more continuations contain plausible target-source patches, so merely distinguishing patch from no patch is no longer sufficient.
- Apply especially when one patched continuation is actively making the modified checkout executable while another stops at `py_compile`, diff inspection, or submission.

Decisive positive evidence:
- A syntactically valid target-source patch combined with concrete progress toward executing the modified checkout. Here, `python setup.py build_ext --inplace` completing successfully and the subsequent local reproduction reaching only a missing `pyparsing` import is stronger directional evidence than syntax checking alone.
- An actual `pickle.dumps` and `pickle.loads` round trip is strongest. Validation should cover both draggable legends and draggable annotations when possible.
- A shared DraggableBase implementation is plausible if it removes the retained canvas from serialized state and handles post-unpickle behavior safely. An owner-level implementation is also plausible if it safely discards or reconstructs transient `_draggable` state for both affected owner paths.
- Continued investigation of unpickle ordering, callback registration, or safe loss of transient dragging is constructive when the visible patch has not yet been behaviorally validated.

Decisive contradictory evidence:
- Submitting a shared-base `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` design after only syntax and diff checks, while treating its callback reconnection and `ref_artist.figure.canvas` access as proven correct.
- Assigning extra correctness merely because a patch removes `canvas`, `cids`, and `background`, calls `disconnect()`, or reconnects several callbacks. Callback IDs are not themselves proof of the reported serialization failure, and cleanup breadth is not behavioral validation.
- Treating mutation during `__getstate__` as automatically desirable. Calling `disconnect()` while serializing can alter the live figure; restoration code can also duplicate or mistime callback registration. These designs may be valid, but require execution evidence rather than rubric assumptions.
- A legend-only owner patch that leaves the separately reported draggable annotation path uncovered, unless another visible shared mechanism covers it.
- Malformed placement, invalid indentation, edits outside the target checkout, or validation against an installed copy instead of the modified source.

Close-looking exclusions:
- Do not require both `__getstate__` and `__setstate__` universally. Safely discarding transient dragging at the owner can satisfy pickling without restoring it, while a design that claims to preserve dragging may legitimately require reconstruction.
- Do not automatically rank a shared DraggableBase patch above separate Legend and Annotation handling. Shared scope is elegant but also introduces unpickle-order and callback-lifecycle obligations.
- Do not treat `py_compile` as behavioral proof. It establishes syntax only.
- Conversely, do not dismiss build or dependency work as generic setup when it follows a preserved source patch and visibly advances execution of that modified checkout. A successful local extension build followed by a narrowly identified missing dependency is meaningful validation progress.
- Do not require one exact state-stripping template, callback policy, or preservation of `use_blit` and `update` if the contract permits safely disabling transient dragging after unpickle.

Rejected misleading rubric or judge bias:
Reject the rule that the most elaborate serialization implementation is necessarily best: both pickle methods, explicit disconnection, removal of every transient-looking attribute, callback reconnection, parameter preservation, and edits to every named class are not mandatory correctness signals. Also reject automatically awarding the highest rank to any shared DraggableBase patch after a syntax check. When plausible patches compete, visible progress toward executing a pickle round trip on the modified checkout is more decisive than static cleanup maximalism.

Abstention boundary:
- If all visible patches are truncated and no continuation has progressed beyond static inspection or syntax checking, do not infer exact semantic correctness from method count or file scope; preserve uncertainty among plausible implementations.
- If one continuation has visibly built and begun executing the modified checkout while another has only statically inspected a similarly plausible patch, directional ranking is justified even before the final round trip.
- If no target-source patch exists, rank only diagnosis and targeting rather than implementation quality.

experiences.title: W042 fix: rank the displayed final patch above test volume
experiences.description: When judging continuations for the Django models.W042 inherited-primary-key fix, verify that the final submission actually displays a unified diff for django/db/models/base.py. Do not let broad regression coverage or a correct working-tree diff outrank a continuation whose final output is only a summary or other non-patch content. Accept equivalent valid patch paths and formatting; the requirement is the final displayed artifact, not a specific filename.
experiences.context: The task changes Model._check_default_pk so an auto-created primary key that is a multi-table-inheritance parent link does not trigger W042, while standalone auto-created primary keys continue to warn. Several continuations share equivalent working-tree fixes and show successful targeted or broad tests. The decisive submission distinction is whether the final completion output contains the actual diff for django/db/models/base.py.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply this rule when continuations have comparable W042 fixes and the visible trajectory reaches final patch generation or completion. Inspect the final completion output itself, not only earlier git diff commands or test results.

Decisive positive evidence: The final output includes a unified diff header targeting django/db/models/base.py and a hunk that adds the parent-link exclusion while preserving the DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD and AppConfig checks. The artifact may be named patch.txt, /tmp/fix.patch, /tmp/final_patch.txt, or another path, and equivalent conditional formatting is valid. A branch with this displayed patch is submission-complete; among such branches, compare behavioral validation and regression coverage.

Contradictory evidence: A final completion signal followed by a prose summary, raw source excerpt, or unrelated diff does not submit the fix. Earlier successful tests and an earlier working-tree git diff do not cure the absence of the target-file diff in the final artifact. A branch that only prints a summary after running broad model or inheritance suites must not outrank a branch that visibly submits the valid target diff merely because it has more test output.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not require the literal filename patch.txt, a particular diff hunk layout, a particular number of changed lines, or a particular implementation spelling. A final cat of any artifact is sufficient if its visible diff header targets django/db/models/base.py and its content contains the valid W042 change. Conversely, do not treat a command that merely creates a patch, an intermediate git diff, or a test pass as final submission evidence unless the final output displays that artifact.

Abstention boundary: If the final submission command or its diff header is truncated and it is impossible to tell whether a target-file patch was displayed, do not infer submission failure from test volume or completion wording; score the branch using the other visible evidence. If no submission step is visible, evaluate implementation and validation only, without inventing a submission-format penalty.

Misleading rubric or judge bias rejected: Reject the bias that the branch with the broadest existing test suite or the most convincing prose summary is automatically best. Submission of the actual target-file patch is a primary requirement; test breadth is only a secondary tiebreaker after valid final artifacts are established. Preserve equivalent correct implementations rather than rewarding a specific patch filename or formatting style.

experiences.title: Resolve bulk_create conflict fields to db_column before backend SQL generation
experiences.description: For QuerySet.bulk_create(update_conflicts=True) issues involving fields whose Python names differ from db_column, rank the data-flow correction above backend-only pattern matching or broad regression-suite counts. The backend SQL methods need database column names, but the public bulk_create API supplies field-name strings; those names must be resolved through model metadata before on_conflict_suffix_sql() quotes them.
experiences.context: The reported SQL uses lowercase Python names such as blacklistid and sectorid in ON CONFLICT and DO UPDATE, while INSERT already uses the mixed-case database columns BlacklistID and SectorID. Visible tracing shows _check_bulk_create_options() obtains Field objects only for validation, while the original update_fields and unique_fields lists continue into InsertQuery and SQLInsertCompiler. The compiler then forwards those lists to PostgreSQL, SQLite, or MySQL operations. The existing bulk_create tests pass but visibly do not define db_column fields, so they are regression coverage rather than proof of this scenario.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply when the task concerns bulk_create(update_conflicts=True), unique_fields or update_fields, and a model has db_column values different from its Python field names. Apply especially when comparing backend operations patches, compiler/query tracing, mock SQL scripts, and the existing bulk_create test suite.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a trajectory that visibly identifies the type and lifetime of these arguments across query.py, InsertQuery, and SQLInsertCompiler, then resolves each requested name with the model field's .column before the backend quotes it. Equivalent valid implementations include converting the lists to Field objects before constructing InsertQuery, converting names to Field.column in SQLInsertCompiler, or another implementation that guarantees every relevant backend receives the actual database column names while preserving the pk alias and normal string API. Credit an end-to-end reproduction that defines fields such as blacklistid = IntegerField(db_column='BlacklistID') and sectorid = IntegerField(db_column='SectorID'), invokes the real SQL-generation or bulk_create path, and shows ON CONFLICT/DO UPDATE or the backend-equivalent clause using BlacklistID and SectorID. Also credit regression tests for ordinary field names, multiple conflict fields, and empty or unsupported conflict targets.

Contradictory evidence: A patch that only replaces map(self.quote_name, update_fields) with map(lambda f: self.quote_name(f.column), update_fields) in backend operations is wrong when the visible upstream path still passes strings; it can raise AttributeError on the real API path. A defensive getattr(f, 'column', f) variant merely avoids that exception and still emits the Python names for string inputs, so it does not fix the reported db_column mismatch. A script that passes mock Field objects directly to backend methods, greps for field.column, or prints hand-constructed SQL is not end-to-end validation. A passing bulk_create suite without any db_column model does not exercise the bug. Do not reward a larger number of backend files, more test output, or a patch that claims success while its own reproduction still produces blacklistid/sectorid.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not require backend operations edits if the compiler or query layer demonstrably supplies Field.column strings and the backend implementation already quotes strings correctly. Do not penalize equivalent implementations that centralize conversion in the compiler rather than duplicating it across PostgreSQL, SQLite, and MySQL. MySQL may only need update-field conversion because its conflict syntax has no explicit unique target, while PostgreSQL and SQLite need both target and update columns. A real backend connection is stronger validation but is not necessary if the source-level data flow and actual compiler-generated SQL are visible.

Misleading rubric/judge rejection: Reject the bias that treats “all three operations.py files use field.column” as a complete fix, or that ranks a broad 50-test suite and mock-field script above a branch that correctly proves the arguments are strings and locates the conversion at the compiler/query boundary. Reject both blanket backend-file-count scoring and blanket test-count scoring; correctness is determined by the actual argument representation and by SQL containing db_column values.

Abstention boundary: If the relevant query.py/compiler data flow or the final diff is truncated, do not conclude that a backend-only patch is correct or incorrect solely from a diff statistic. If the test backend is not visible, do not infer cross-backend success. If only source inspection is visible, treat the implementation as plausible but leave behavioral validation incomplete unless actual generated SQL or a real test assertion is shown.

experiences.title: For the Product Add bug, observed executable diagnosis outranks write-only target edits
experiences.description: When a Product evaluation branch has cleanly reproduced and localized the additive-term defect, rank it above a branch that merely ran a target replacement script without displaying or executing the resulting source. A command that prints “replacement successful” is intent-level evidence, not proof of a usable implementation.
experiences.context: The relevant Product evaluation path handles an additive term by separately evaluating its addends and combining the results with sum, which incorrectly assumes that a product distributes over addition. Python compatibility failures involving Mapping, MutableSet, and Callable can obscure this defect. At a paused pre-validation state, the key distinction is whether the code is observably executable and the mathematical mechanism is demonstrated, not whether a write command nominally mentioned the target method.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply this rule when branches investigating the Product additive-term defect diverge between (a) a clean, executable reproduction with causal localization and (b) a target-file replacement command whose result has not been read back or executed. It also applies when broad compatibility substitutions visibly damage the codebase.

Decisive positive evidence: Strongly credit a branch that narrowly repairs the compatibility blockers, reaches a return-code-zero execution, and prints concrete pre-fix evidence such as n=1 producing 2, n=2 producing 9/2 instead of 15/2, and larger nontrivial values disagreeing with manually constructed products. Inspection of the term.is_Add branch together with the explanation that `sum([self._eval_product(...) ...])` incorrectly distributes a product over addition establishes the task-specific mechanism. This is verified diagnosis and a sound platform for the next edit.

Decisive contradictory evidence: A replacement script that only reports “Fix applied successfully” or “Replacement successful” does not establish that the resulting method is syntactically valid, correctly indented, or semantically appropriate. If there is no subsequent display of the modified block, successful import, or behavioral run, do not score it as a completed or validated implementation. Broad source-wide substitutions are stronger negative evidence when they insert imports inside control-flow blocks and produce an observed IndentationError; touching many files or the target file does not offset an unusable source state.

Ranking rule: A successful, multi-case pre-fix reproduction with exact causal localization should outrank an unobserved write-only target edit. A visibly corrupted state should rank below focused compatibility work. Reserve higher implementation credit for an observed surgical change to the Add branch, and reserve the highest credit for successful post-edit execution showing either the correct finite value, an appropriately unevaluated Product, or another mathematically equivalent representation such as q-Pochhammer. Preserve all such valid implementations rather than requiring one textual patch.

Close-looking exclusions: Pre-fix outputs for n=2, n=3, and n=4 are diagnosis evidence, not fix validation. Conversely, do not automatically demote a surgical target edit merely because full regression tests are still pending: if the modified source is visibly shown, structurally sound, and successfully imports, it is genuine implementation progress. Focused Mapping, MutableSet, or Callable repairs are legitimate prerequisite work, but they remain below successful reproduction and target-specific diagnosis unless they also enable those observations. A last-step edit command with no readback is weaker than an already observed modified method.

Misleading rubric or judge bias to reject: Explicitly reject the bias that any command writing to the target method must outrank executable reproduction and causal localization. Also reject treating a script’s self-reported success as visible patch evidence, treating pre-fix multi-case output as post-fix validation, or assigning all compatibility-blocked branches the same minimum score despite a distinction between focused unblocking and source-corrupting global replacement.

Abstention boundary: If no branch reaches successful execution and no branch displays the resulting target source or an observed post-edit failure, do not choose between a merely intended target edit and focused compatibility work. Likewise, if all branches only issue unverified write commands, preserve uncertainty until source readback, import behavior, or task-specific execution becomes visible.

experiences.title: Prefer the visible per-output classes_ contract repair over a generic validation workaround
experiences.description: When `MultiOutputClassifier.predict_proba` visibly returns a list ordered by `estimators_`, exposing `classes_` as the correspondingly ordered list of fitted estimators' class arrays is a direct repair of the missing estimator contract. A property or fit-time assignment implementing that structure must not be penalized merely because it changes `multioutput.py` rather than `_validation.py`. In a paused comparison, an implemented property plus patch creation can outrank completed generic validation-site edits that have only syntax or mock-logic checks and never exercise the reported call.
experiences.context: The affected validation code indexes `classes_[i_label]` alongside the i-th probability array. Source inspection shows that `MultiOutputClassifier.predict_proba` constructs its result by iterating over `self.estimators_`, while the classifier lacks the top-level `classes_` attribute referenced by its probability-output contract. The visible alternatives include a classifier-specific `classes_` property returning each fitted estimator's classes and broader validation-site logic that treats any estimator with `estimators_` as a multi-output classifier.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply this rule when comparing fixes for the `cross_val_predict(..., method='predict_proba')` failure and the visible state shows either a `MultiOutputClassifier.classes_` implementation or validation-site extraction from `estimators_`.

Decisive positive evidence: A property such as `classes_` that calls `check_is_fitted(self)` and returns `[estimator.classes_ for estimator in self.estimators_]` is structurally aligned with `predict_proba`, which returns one probability array for each estimator in that same order. Assigning the same list during `fit` is an equivalent valid implementation. Matching attribute documentation and successful patch-file creation strengthen this evidence. Integer indexing of this list is exactly what `classes_[i_label]` requires.

Contradictory evidence: Penalize an estimator-level adapter only if it flattens the class arrays, changes their order, derives them from objects other than the fitted per-output estimators, or exposes a length inconsistent with the probability list. A generic validation change based solely on the presence of `estimators_` is weaker when it assumes every ensemble-like estimator maps estimators one-to-one to list-valued outputs. Syntax checks and standalone mock tests do not resolve that semantic breadth and do not demonstrate the reported call.

Close-looking exclusions: An existing `classes_` assignment in another multi-output class does not mean `MultiOutputClassifier` already exposes the attribute; inspect the enclosing class. A comment or docstring mentioning `classes_` without a visible property or fit assignment is not an implementation. Conversely, do not claim that a list-valued `classes_` cannot satisfy `classes_[i_label]`: list indexing returns the corresponding class array. A carefully scoped validation-site implementation can also be valid, so do not reject it solely for its location; however, it should not outrank the visible classifier-specific contract repair merely because it has a completed submission or more mock-test output.

Paused-submission boundary: Successful `git diff ... > patch.txt` establishes that a patch artifact was prepared, but not that final submission was displayed. Treat that as pending submission evidence, not as a correctness defect. If the property body or fit assignment is not visible and only future intent is stated, rank it below an implemented change and abstain on whether it will ultimately be correct. If no relevant edit is visible in any branch, do not infer correctness from discussion alone.

Reject the misleading rubric or judge bias: Reject any rule asserting that `_validation.py` is the only correct target or that adding a list of per-estimator class arrays cannot fix `classes_[i_label]`. Also reject ranking a generic workaround highest solely because it reached a final patch display or ran more isolated checks while the direct, visibly implemented estimator contract repair is paused after creating its patch file.

experiences.title: Trace NdarrayMixin re-exports before calling the import orphaned
experiences.description: When changing Table's structured-array handling, do not rank a patch higher merely because it removes an apparently unused NdarrayMixin import. The import may be the source used by astropy.table.__init__.py to expose NdarrayMixin publicly. Local grep results are insufficient evidence for safe deletion; follow the import graph and preserve the public API unless the re-export is moved and verified.
experiences.context: Use for the structured ndarray transition in astropy/table/table.py when a branch removes the auto-conversion block and considers deleting the NdarrayMixin import. The visible trajectories show both the conversion removal and an import cleanup, while the package initializer visibly references NdarrayMixin. The task also describes a two-phase lifecycle, so warning-versus-removal must be judged according to the explicit release phase, not used as a substitute for checking import compatibility.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Trigger when a visible patch removes the structured-array conversion and either deletes `from .ndarray_mixin import NdarrayMixin` or claims that import cleanup is required because table.py has no remaining direct use.

Decisive positive evidence: The patch removes or phases the conversion according to the task's explicit lifecycle, while retaining the import when astropy.table.__init__.py still obtains NdarrayMixin from table.py. Alternatively, deleting the import is valid only when the patch also updates the public re-export to import from the defining module and visibly verifies `from astropy.table import NdarrayMixin` or equivalent package-level compatibility. Targeted checks should cover structured-array initialization and existing Column/mixin paths; a syntax-only check is not enough to establish import compatibility.

Contradictory evidence: Deleting the table.py import solely because `grep` finds no local use, while the initializer still imports or re-exports NdarrayMixin through table.py, is a public-import regression and must outweigh cosmetic orphaned-import cleanup. Do not reward a branch for stating that the symbol is used elsewhere unless it traces the actual import source and updates it if necessary. Also do not treat a warning-only patch as equivalent to the requested 5.2 removal when the visible task phase is 5.2; conversely, do not treat immediate removal as equivalent to the 5.1 warning phase when the task explicitly requires retaining the old behavior during deprecation.

Close-looking exclusions: Retaining the import is not sufficient if the conversion block or required warning behavior is otherwise wrong. Removing the import can be equivalent if the initializer's import is explicitly redirected to astropy.table.ndarray_mixin and the public import is tested. A different warning message or formatting is acceptable when it conveys the required migration and uses an appropriate stacklevel. Do not penalize an implementation for harmlessly retaining an unused import when it preserves the public API and satisfies the requested behavior.

Abstention boundary: If the visible diff does not show the import source, the package initializer is not inspectable, the release phase is ambiguous, or the public import result is unavailable, do not infer that the import is safe or unsafe to delete. Score only the visible behavioral change and preserve uncertainty about package-level compatibility.

experiences.title: Gate even-power transformations by their integer domain, not only by safe comparisons
experiences.description: When an even-power transformation crashes while comparing a complex exponent, distinguish a domain guard from a comparison-only repair. If the remaining algorithm uses parity, integer division, and perfect-power decomposition, guarding the entire path to exponents known to be integers is stronger than merely replacing the two throwing comparisons with safe sign properties.
experiences.context: In an exponent transformation helper, direct `< 0` and `> max` comparisons reject a complex exponent. Visible fixes either return early when the exponent is not known to be an integer or replace those comparisons with `is_negative` and an `is_positive` difference check. After the comparisons, the helper applies `% 2`, `// 2`, and `perfect_power`, and its documentation describes even powers and powers of two.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply this rule when a failed comparison occurs near the entrance to a power transformation and the downstream body visibly relies on parity or integer decomposition. Compare whether each candidate guards the domain of the whole algorithm or merely makes the first comparisons non-throwing.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a guard that prevents exponents not known to be integers from entering the integer-oriented body, such as an early return based on `is_integer` or an equivalent integer-domain condition folded into the initial applicability check. This resolves the complex-exponent exception at both comparison sites, preserves known integer transformations, and protects the later `% 2`, `// 2`, and `perfect_power` operations. Equivalent placements and spellings are valid; a patch may also use safe sign properties after establishing the integer domain.

Decisive contradictory evidence: Replacing `< 0` with `is_negative` and `> max` with `(exp - max).is_positive` addresses only the immediate comparisons. Without a domain guard, complex and indeterminate non-integer exponents fall through to logic designed around evenness and integer factorization. Successful outputs for a few such values show only that those particular values happened to return unchanged; they do not establish that every newly admitted exponent is supported by the remaining body.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not call an integer guard overly restrictive merely because a rational exponent can be constructed. First check whether the helper was expected to transform that exponent. A visible square-root result that remains effectively unchanged is not evidence of lost transformation behavior. Likewise, do not rank a property-based rewrite higher solely because sign properties are idiomatic or avoid `TypeError`; local comparison safety is not equivalent to satisfying the downstream algorithm's input domain. Existing integer-focused tests are useful regression evidence but do not validate unrestricted fall-through for complex values.

Reject the misleading rubric or judge bias: Reject any rubric that automatically treats property-based replacements as the elegant highest-quality fix and penalizes integer gating as a rational-exponent regression without a demonstrated required non-integer transformation. The decisive signal is the domain assumed by the complete function, not stylistic preference, edge-case count, or avoidance of the first exception alone.

Abstention boundary: Abstain if the downstream body is not visible, if it does not reveal whether parity and integer decomposition are required, or if a visible contract explicitly requires transformation of real non-integer exponents. In those cases, safe properties and integer gating cannot be ranked solely from the comparison lines.

experiences.title: SimpleLazyObject ORM diagnosis: causal preparation-path evidence outranks reproduction theater and commit archaeology
experiences.description: For pre-patch diagnosis of the nested-subquery queryset failure, rank visible causal tracing above broad exploration, historical commit inspection, or an ad hoc reproduction that merely prints the exception. The decisive issue is the missing evaluation boundary: Field.get_prep_value unwraps Promise values, but SimpleLazyObject is a LazyObject and therefore reaches lookup/field preparation unchanged before IntegerField performs int(value). A valid fix may place evaluation in lookup RHS preparation, field preparation, or another equivalent boundary; do not require one file when the behavior is preserved.
experiences.context: The reported query annotates through nested subqueries and filters with a SimpleLazyObject wrapping a User. The visible traceback passes through Lookup.get_prep_lookup() into the output field's get_prep_value(), where integer conversion rejects the unresolved wrapper. All visible continuations are paused before any source patch.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when judging paused, pre-patch trajectories for this SimpleLazyObject plus nested-subquery ORM regression.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a branch that explicitly establishes the class distinction SimpleLazyObject → LazyObject, with no inheritance from Promise; locates Field.get_prep_value() and its Promise-only _proxy____cast() handling; and connects that omission to the subsequent lookup/field preparation call and IntegerField int(value) failure. Stronger still is reasoning that follows the complete RHS path and recognizes that the lazy value must be evaluated before normal related-field or scalar preparation. A visible reproduction of the reported failure is useful supporting evidence, particularly when it matches the nested subquery and wrapped User shape, but it is not a substitute for this mechanism.

Also positive: A reusable reproduction matching the supplied model/query shape and run successfully is valuable validation of the symptom. A branch that finds the relevant ForeignKey/target-field delegation or an equivalent preparation boundary should receive credit even if it proposes a different valid implementation location, provided it preserves ordinary values and existing Promise behavior.

Contradictory evidence: Do not treat an ad hoc script that prints the TypeError as complete diagnosis when the branch does not explain why Promise handling misses SimpleLazyObject or incorrectly concludes that the mere call site in lookups.py is the fix. Do not count a script stopped by missing dependencies as reproduction output. Do not treat merely creating a test file, inspecting a commit, or listing more files as evidence that the bug was reproduced or causally understood. Exploration of encoding helpers or other Promise/string utilities is contradictory when presented as the fix path for a lazy model object.

Close-looking exclusions: Finding the Promise check alone is relevant but incomplete; without verifying that SimpleLazyObject is not a Promise, do not infer the inheritance diagnosis. Finding LazyObject mechanics alone is also incomplete unless the branch connects them to the field-preparation pipeline. A successful reproduction can outrank pure file listing for symptom evidence, but it must not outrank an explicit causal diagnosis merely because its output contains a more exact exception string. Conversely, a branch that clearly identifies the inheritance and preparation gap remains meaningful even if its later test attempt fails during environment setup. Do not penalize a valid fix boundary solely because it is in lookup preparation rather than Field.get_prep_value, or vice versa.

Misleading rubric or judge-bias rejection: Reject the bias that the branch with the most files explored, the historical regression commit, or the most explicit ad hoc error print is automatically the best diagnosis. Those signals are secondary to identifying the Promise-versus-LazyObject mismatch and the precise preparation chain. Also reject the opposite bias that an environment-blocked reproduction erases prior source-based causal reasoning; score visible diagnosis and reproduction separately.

Abstention boundary: If a paused prefix contains only directory listings or broad searches and has not visibly found the Promise check, the LazyObject inheritance, the preparation call, or a meaningful reproduction result, make no fine-grained ranking claim. If a branch has only created a script or has stopped before its output, do not infer what it would reproduce. If a source diff or post-change test appears, switch from this pre-patch hierarchy to evaluating the implementation and its validation.

experiences.title: For paused xr.where repairs, visible syntax contradictions override edit recency
experiences.description: During the first diagnosis-to-edit round of an `xr.where` attribute-loss repair, first demote any visibly invalid or duplicated `apply_ufunc` call. An unverified final substitution is not implementation evidence and must not outrank a clean prefix that identifies the active top-level call, confirms the attribute-retention mechanism, and prepares focused coverage.
experiences.context: The top-level `where` path in `xarray/core/computation.py` calls `apply_ufunc`. Visible prefixes include clean mechanism analysis, focused test discovery, a keyword inserted before positional arguments, a duplicated argument block, and a final line-number edit whose resulting source is not shown. Baseline output also demonstrates attribute loss and dtype promotion as separate observations.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Apply at a paused, first-round snapshot for top-level `xr.where` attribute preservation when visible prefixes differ in source correctness, active-call analysis, focused test preparation, or verification of an edit. This rule applies before any prefix has established a complete post-change behavioral pass.

Highest-weight hard discriminator: Visible semantic or syntactic contradiction takes precedence over edit activity. An `apply_ufunc` call that places a keyword before remaining positional arguments is invalid Python. A call that repeats the callable, `cond`, `x`, `y`, or the existing option block is structurally corrupt. Either state must rank below a clean prefix with exact active-call reasoning, regardless of how confidently the edit was described or how recently it was made.

Decisive positive evidence: Require a concrete connection between the public top-level function and its active call in `xarray/core/computation.py`, together with recognition that `apply_ufunc` supports attribute retention. Strong visible readiness also includes preserving a syntactically clean call and locating the focused `test_where` area in `xarray/tests/test_computation.py` for a regression assertion. A displayed valid modification is stronger still when all positional arguments remain intact and the retention behavior is configured inside the call. Preserve equivalent implementations: do not require one exact textual edit or keyword order among keyword arguments; accept any compatible implementation that preserves attributes for the ordinary three-argument API without corrupting the call or imposing an incompatible interface change.
